title.zh: 卷254 列傳四十一 赉塔 穆占 莽依图 佛尼埒 毕力克图 阿密达 拉哈达 根特 席卜臣
title.en: Volume 254 Biographies 41: Lai Ta, Mu Zhan, Mang Yi Tu, Fu Ni Lie, Bi Liketu, A Mi Da, La Ha Da, Gen Te, Xi Bochen
title.raw: 卷254 列傳四十一 赉塔 穆占 莽依图 佛尼埒 毕力克图 阿密达 拉哈达 根特 席卜臣

sentences.zh: 拉哈達察哈泰根特華善席卜臣希爾根}}賚塔，那穆都魯氏，滿洲正白旗人，康古里第四子。

translations.literal: Laita, of the Namuduru clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner and the fourth son of Kanguli.
translations.idiomatic: Laita, of the Namuduru clan, belonged to the Plain White Banner and was the fourth son of Kanguli.

sentences.zh: 年十四，授三等侍衛。

translations.literal: At age fourteen he was appointed third-class imperial guard.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he received appointment as a third-class imperial guard.

sentences.zh: 坐事免。

translations.literal: He was dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: He was removed from office for misconduct.

sentences.zh: 崇德時，從伐明，圍錦州，擊松山、杏山敵兵，屢有斬獲。

translations.literal: In the Chongde era he followed the campaign against Ming, besieged Jinzhou, and struck enemy forces at Songshan and Xingshan, repeatedly taking heads.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongde reign he joined the expedition against Ming, helped besiege Jinzhou, and fought enemy troops at Songshan and Xingshan, winning repeated victories in the field.

sentences.zh: 攻新城、高陽、霸州、壽光、博興，並先登，身中五創。

translations.literal: Attacking Xincheng, Gaoyang, Bazhou, Shouguang, and Boxing, he was first to scale the walls each time and received five wounds.
translations.idiomatic: In assaults on Xincheng, Gaoyang, Bazhou, Shouguang, and Boxing he was always first over the wall and took five wounds in the process.

sentences.zh: 被賞賚，授前鋒侍衛。

translations.literal: He was rewarded and appointed vanguard guard.
translations.idiomatic: He received rewards and was named a vanguard guard.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，從討李自成，敗之一片石，追至安肅、慶都。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi he followed the campaign against Li Zicheng, defeated him at Yipianshi, and pursued to Ansu and Qingdu.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shunzhi he marched against Li Zicheng, routed him at Yipianshi, and pursued him as far as Ansu and Qingdu.

sentences.zh: 授巴牙喇甲喇章京。

translations.literal: He was appointed company commander of the Vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a Vanguard company commander.

sentences.zh: 從豫親王多鐸轉戰河南、陝西，頻有功。

translations.literal: Following Prince of Yu Dorgon he fought through Henan and Shaanxi and repeatedly distinguished himself.
translations.idiomatic: Serving under Prince of Yu Dorgon, he campaigned across Henan and Shaanxi and won distinction again and again.

sentences.zh: 二年，移師江南，克揚州，下江寧，追敗明福王於蕪湖，予拖沙喇哈番。

translations.literal: In the second year the army shifted to Jiangnan, took Yangzhou, captured Jiangning, pursued and defeated the Ming Prince of Fu at Wuhu, and he was granted the hereditary rank of captain.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the army turned south: Yangzhou fell, Jiangning was taken, and the Ming Prince of Fu was routed at Wuhu; Laita was granted a hereditary captaincy.

sentences.zh: 三年，從端重親王博洛下福建，明唐王奔汀州，賚塔率師攻破其城，進拜他喇布勒哈番。

translations.literal: In the third year he followed Prince Duanzhong Bolo into Fujian; the Ming Prince of Tang fled to Tingzhou, and Laita led troops that stormed the city and was advanced to deputy company commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he followed Prince Duanzhong Bolo into Fujian. When the Ming Prince of Tang fled to Tingzhou, Laita led the force that took the city and was promoted to deputy company commander.

sentences.zh: 明桂王據湖南。

translations.literal: The Ming Prince of Gui held Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming Prince of Gui still held Hunan.

sentences.zh: 六年，從鄭親王濟爾哈朗進衡州，戰敗明將陶養用、胡一清；

translations.literal: In the sixth year he followed Prince of Zheng Jirhalang to Hengzhou and defeated the Ming generals Tao Yangyong and Hu Yiqing;
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he marched with Prince of Zheng Jirhalang on Hengzhou and defeated the Ming generals Tao Yangyong and Hu Yiqing;

sentences.zh: 克祁陽，复戰敗明將周進唐、王進才及一清；

translations.literal: took Qiyang, and again defeated the Ming generals Zhou Jintang, Wang Jincai, and Yiqing;
translations.idiomatic: captured Qiyang, then again defeated Zhou Jintang, Wang Jincai, and Hu Yiqing;

sentences.zh: 又戰敗明將譚弘，取道州；

translations.literal: again defeated the Ming general Tan Hong and took Daozhou;
translations.idiomatic: routed the Ming general Tan Hong and seized Daozhou;

sentences.zh: 又戰敗一清及明將焦璉，取全州。

translations.literal: again defeated Yiqing and the Ming general Jiao Lian, and took Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: and finally defeated Hu Yiqing and the Ming general Jiao Lian and took Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 累晉二等阿達哈哈番兼世管佐領。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to second-class commandant with hereditary assistant commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in stages to second-class commandant and hereditary assistant commandant of his company.

sentences.zh: 十一年，明將李定國犯廣東，從珠瑪喇解新會圍，進三等阿思哈尼哈番，擢巴牙喇纛章京。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the Ming general Li Dingguo invaded Guangdong; following Zhumala he relieved the siege of Xinhui, was advanced to third-class commandant-in-chief, and was promoted Vanguard banner commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, when the Ming general Li Dingguo struck Guangdong, he served under Zhumala to lift the siege of Xinhui, was raised to third-class commandant-in-chief, and became Vanguard banner commander.

sentences.zh: 十六年，鄭成功窺江寧，從安南將軍達素討之。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year Zheng Chenggong threatened Jiangning; he followed Pacification General of Annan Dasu to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year Zheng Chenggong menaced Jiangning, and Laita marched with Pacification General of Annan Dasu against him.

sentences.zh: 比至，成功已敗遁，遂引兵下福建。

translations.literal: By the time they arrived, Chenggong had already been defeated and fled, so the army was led down into Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: When they arrived Chenggong had already been beaten and had fled, so the army continued into Fujian.

sentences.zh: 十七年，戰廈門，師失利，坐免官，奪世職。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year they fought at Xiamen; the army suffered defeat, and he was dismissed and stripped of his hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year the army was defeated at Xiamen; he lost his post and his hereditary rank.

sentences.zh: 康熙二年，署前鋒統領。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kangxi he acted as vanguard commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kangxi he served as acting vanguard commander.

sentences.zh: 擊李來亨等於茅麓山，數戰皆克。

translations.literal: He attacked Li Laiheng and others at Maolu Mountain and won every engagement.
translations.idiomatic: At Maolu Mountain he fought Li Laiheng and his followers and won every battle.

sentences.zh: 八年，擢正白旗蒙古都統。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was promoted Mongol lieutenant-general of the Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was made Mongol lieutenant-general of the Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 十三年，耿精忠叛，遣其將馬九玉、曾養性、白顯忠分三道寇浙江。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Geng Jingzhong rebelled and sent his generals Ma Jiuyu, Zeng Yangxing, and Bai Xianzhong in three columns to raid Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Geng Jingzhong rose in rebellion and sent Ma Jiuyu, Zeng Yangxing, and Bai Xianzhong against Zhejiang in three columns.

sentences.zh: 授賚塔平南將軍，赴援。

translations.literal: Laita was appointed Pacification General of the South and sent to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: Laita was named Pacification General of the South and marched to their aid.

sentences.zh: 寇犯金華，遣諸將瑪哈​​達、雅塔里、拉哈等擊走之，复義烏、諸暨。

translations.literal: When the rebels struck Jinhua he sent the generals Mahada, Yatali, Laha, and others to drive them off and recovered Yiwu and Zhuji.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels attacked Jinhua he sent Mahada, Yatali, Laha, and others to repulse them and recovered Yiwu and Zhuji.

sentences.zh: 精忠將王國斌屯金、衢接壤處，為群寇聲援。

translations.literal: Jingzhong's general Wang Guobin encamped on the border of Jinhua and Quzhou to support the rebel bands.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhong's general Wang Guobin held the Jinhua–Quzhou border to back the other rebel forces.

sentences.zh: 賚塔與總督李之芳駐衢州，精忠將周列擁眾二萬自常山入。

translations.literal: Laita and Governor Li Zhifang were stationed at Quzhou when Jingzhong's general Zhou Lie entered from Changshan with twenty thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Laita and Governor Li Zhifang were at Quzhou when Jingzhong's general Zhou Lie came down from Changshan with twenty thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 賚塔遣瑚圖要之焦園，俘斬過半。

translations.literal: Laita sent Hutu to intercept them at Jiaoyuan; more than half were captured or killed.
translations.idiomatic: Laita sent Hutu to block them at Jiaoyuan and killed or captured more than half their force.

sentences.zh: 精忠將桑明率眾五萬犯衢州，迎擊，斬級萬餘。

translations.literal: Jingzhong's general Sang Ming led fifty thousand men against Quzhou; meeting them in battle, more than ten thousand heads were taken.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingzhong's general Sang Ming attacked Quzhou with fifty thousand men, Laita met him in battle and took more than ten thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 十四年，督兵擊九玉，五戰皆捷，又破其將李廷魁，焚所屯木城。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he directed troops against Jiuyu, won five battles in succession, also defeated his general Li Tingkui, and burned the wooden stockade where they were encamped.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he led the attack on Jiuyu, won five straight engagements, routed his general Li Tingkui, and burned the wooden fort where the rebels had camped.

sentences.zh: 康親王杰書軍至衢州，賚塔依例歸將軍印，以都統參贊軍務。

translations.literal: When Prince Kang Jieshu's army reached Quzhou, Laita returned the general's seal as prescribed and served as lieutenant-general assisting in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Kang Jieshu arrived at Quzhou, Laita surrendered the general's seal as regulations required and served as lieutenant-general on the staff.

sentences.zh: 時九玉退據九龍山，分萬人扼大溪灘護糧運。

translations.literal: Jiuyu had withdrawn to Jiulong Mountain and detached ten thousand men to hold Daxitan and protect grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuyu had fallen back to Jiulong Mountain and posted ten thousand men at Daxitan to guard his supply lines.

sentences.zh: 傑書令賚塔攻之，即夕遣兵涉河，直搗九玉營，破之。

translations.literal: Jieshu ordered Laita to attack; that same evening troops were sent across the river straight into Jiuyu's camp and broke it.
translations.idiomatic: Jieshu ordered Laita to strike; that night troops crossed the river, fell on Jiuyu's camp, and routed it.

sentences.zh: 九玉僅以三十騎遁，遂復常山。

translations.literal: Jiuyu escaped with only thirty horsemen, and Changshan was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuyu fled with only thirty horsemen, and Changshan was taken back.

sentences.zh: 率瑪哈達等破仙霞關，拔浦城；

translations.literal: Leading Mahada and others he broke Xianxia Pass and took Pucheng;
translations.idiomatic: He led Mahada and others through Xianxia Pass and captured Pucheng;

sentences.zh: 又與吉勒塔布敗賊建陽，克之。

translations.literal: and with Jiletabu defeated the rebels at Jianyang and took the city.
translations.idiomatic: then with Jiletabu defeated the rebels at Jianyang and took the city.

sentences.zh: 進取建寧，薄延平，精忠乃迎降。

translations.literal: Advancing on Jianning and pressing Yanping, Jingzhong then came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: As the army advanced on Jianning and closed on Yanping, Jingzhong at last submitted.

sentences.zh: 其時漳、泉、興化並為鄭錦所據，錦，成功子也。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang, Quan, and Xinghua were all held by Zheng Jing—Jing being Chenggong's son.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangzhou, Quanzhou, and Xinghua were then all held by Zheng Jing, Chenggong's son.

sentences.zh: 精忠導貝子傅拉塔軍攻錦。

translations.literal: Jingzhong guided the army of the prince's son Fulata against Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhong guided Prince Fulata's army against Zheng Jing.

sentences.zh: 十六年，與寧海將軍拉哈達復興化，降仙遊。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, with Pacification General of Ninghai Lahada, he recovered Xinghua and received the surrender of Xianyou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he and Pacification General of Ninghai Lahada retook Xinghua and accepted the surrender of Xianyou.

sentences.zh: 進討叛將劉進忠於潮州，進忠亦降。

translations.literal: Advancing against the rebel general Liu Jinzhong at Chaozhou, Jinzhong also surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He marched on the rebel Liu Jinzhong at Chaozhou, and Jinzhong submitted as well.

sentences.zh: 康親王杰書奏仍授賚塔平南將軍，守潮州。

translations.literal: Prince Kang Jieshu memorialized that Laita again be made Pacification General of the South to guard Chaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Kang Jieshu recommended that Laita again be named Pacification General of the South and left to hold Chaozhou.

sentences.zh: 十七年，錦將劉國軒入犯泉州，與總督姚啟聖會師赴援，复長泰，戰漳州，破敵。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Jing's general Liu Guoxuan invaded Quanzhou; joining Governor Yao Qisheng in relief, he recovered Changtai, fought at Zhangzhou, and defeated the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Liu Guoxuan, a general of Zheng Jing, struck Quanzhou; Laita united with Governor Yao Qisheng to relieve the city, retook Changtai, fought at Zhangzhou, and routed the foe.

sentences.zh: 十八年，國軒復入犯，迎擊，敗走。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Guoxuan invaded again; meeting him in battle, Laita drove him off in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year Guoxuan invaded again; Laita met him and put him to flight.

sentences.zh: 十九年，克海澄，錦還台灣。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year Haicheng was taken and Jing returned to Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year Haicheng fell and Zheng Jing withdrew to Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 授賚塔本旗滿洲都統，守潮州如故。

translations.literal: Laita was appointed Manchu lieutenant-general of his own banner and continued to guard Chaozhou as before.
translations.idiomatic: Laita was made Manchu lieutenant-general of his banner while remaining in charge of Chaozhou.

sentences.zh: 尚之信之降也，仍懷貳志，返廣東，复抗命。

translations.literal: When Shang Zhixin surrendered he still harbored disloyal intent; returning to Guangdong, he again defied orders.
translations.idiomatic: Though Shang Zhixin had submitted, he still nursed treacherous designs; back in Guangdong he once more defied the throne.

sentences.zh: 都統王國棟首告，詔賚塔撫慰。

translations.literal: Lieutenant-general Wang Guodong was first to report it; an edict ordered Laita to reassure him.
translations.idiomatic: Lieutenant-general Wang Guodong was the first to expose him; the court ordered Laita to reassure Zhixin.

sentences.zh: 之信已殺國棟反，賚塔率兵討擒之。

translations.literal: Zhixin had already killed Guodong and rebelled; Laita led troops to suppress and capture him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixin had murdered Guodong and risen in revolt; Laita marched out, defeated him, and took him prisoner.

sentences.zh: 時吳世璠尚據雲南，大將軍貝子彰泰自湖南下貴州，上授賚塔平南大將軍，督滿、漢諸軍自廣西入雲南。

translations.literal: Wu Shifan still held Yunnan; Grand General Prince Zhangtai descended on Guizhou from Hunan, and the emperor appointed Laita Grand Pacification General of the South to command Manchu and Han forces into Yunnan from Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shifan still held Yunnan while Grand General Prince Zhangtai advanced on Guizhou from Hunan. The emperor named Laita Grand Pacification General of the South and gave him command of Manchu and Han troops entering Yunnan from Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 賚塔師自田州、泗城道西隆，迭戰皆捷。

translations.literal: Laita's army marched from Tianzhou and Sicheng toward Xilong by way of repeated victories.
translations.idiomatic: Laita's column moved from Tianzhou and Sicheng toward Xilong, winning every engagement along the way.

sentences.zh: 石門坎者去安籠三十里，地峻★C7，世璠將何繼祖等擁眾拒守。

translations.literal: Shimenkan lies thirty li from Anlong; the ground is steep and rugged, and Shifan's generals He Jizu and others held it with a large force.
translations.idiomatic: Shimenkan, thirty li from Anlong, was steep and difficult country; Shifan's generals He Jizu and others barred the pass with a large army.

sentences.zh: 賚塔令諸將希福、勒貝、瑪奇等率師前進，而別與總督金光祖等分兵自間道躡其後。

translations.literal: Laita ordered the generals Xifu, Lebei, Maqi, and others to advance while he himself, with Governor Jinguangzu and others, detached troops to come up behind by a hidden route.
translations.idiomatic: Laita sent Xifu, Lebei, Maqi, and others forward while he and Governor Jinguangzu took a detachment along a back trail to strike from behind.

sentences.zh: 二十年元旦，度賊無備，飭前軍進攻；

translations.literal: On New Year's Day of the twentieth year, judging the rebels unprepared, he ordered the vanguard to attack;
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day of the twentieth year, reckoning the rebels off guard, he ordered the vanguard forward;

sentences.zh: 繼祖等倉卒出禦，後軍攀險上，前後夾擊，遂奪其隘口，復安籠所。

translations.literal: Jizu and others rushed out to meet them; the rear army climbed the heights, and front and rear struck together, seizing the pass and recovering Anlong post.
translations.idiomatic: Jizu and his men rushed out to fight; Laita's rear column scaled the heights, and the two wings crushed the rebels, took the pass, and recovered Anlong.

sentences.zh: 繼祖復與詹養、王有功等以二萬人守黃草壩。

translations.literal: Jizu again, with Zhan Yang, Wang Yougong, and others, held Huangcaoba with twenty thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Jizu fell back with Zhan Yang, Wang Yougong, and others to hold Huangcaoba with twenty thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 賚塔督諸軍奮擊，自卯至未，破壘二十二，俘養、有功及其眾千餘，並獲其像、馬。

translations.literal: Laita directed the armies in fierce assault from the hour mao to the hour wei, broke twenty-two stockades, captured Yang, Yougong, and more than a thousand of their followers, and also took their idols and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Laita led a furious assault from morning until mid-afternoon, stormed twenty-two stockades, captured Yang and Yougong with more than a thousand of their men, and seized their idols and horses as well.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，上以賚塔自廣西深入，先諸軍至，敗敵，溫詔嘉獎。

translations.literal: When victory was reported, the emperor noted that Laita had penetrated deep from Guangxi, reached the front before the other armies, and defeated the enemy, and sent a warm edict of praise.
translations.idiomatic: News of the victory brought a warm edict of praise: the emperor noted that Laita had pushed deep from Guangxi, arrived ahead of the other columns, and broken the enemy first.

sentences.zh: 師至曲靖，遣諸將希福、瑪奇、碩塔等分道取霑益、雲龍、嵩明諸州及易龍所、楊林城。

translations.literal: The army reached Qujing and sent the generals Xifu, Maqi, Shuota, and others in separate columns to take Zhanyi, Yunlong, Songming, and other prefectures, as well as Yilong post and Yanglin city.
translations.idiomatic: At Qujing he dispatched Xifu, Maqi, Shuota, and others in separate columns to seize Zhanyi, Yunlong, Songming, and other prefectures, along with Yilong post and Yanglin.

sentences.zh: 彰泰師自貴州至，兩軍合。

translations.literal: Zhangtai's army arrived from Guizhou and the two forces united.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangtai's army came up from Guizhou and the two hosts joined.

sentences.zh: 未至會城三十里，世璠遣郭壯圖等迎戰，列象陣，彰泰軍其左，賚塔軍其右，自卯至午，賊五卻五進，殊死戰。

translations.literal: Thirty li short of the provincial capital, Shifan sent Guo Zhuangtu and others to give battle in an elephant formation; Zhangtai's army was on the left and Laita's on the right; from mao to wu the rebels fell back five times and advanced five times in desperate fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty li from the provincial capital, Shifan sent Guo Zhuangtu and others to meet them with war elephants; Zhangtai held the left and Laita the right. From morning until noon the rebels gave ground and surged back five times in a savage fight.

sentences.zh: 過金汁河，象反踐，陣亂，師乘之，大潰，進屯城東歸化寺。

translations.literal: Crossing the Jinzhijiang, the elephants turned and trampled their own side; the formation broke, the army pressed the advantage, the enemy collapsed in rout, and the troops encamped east of the city at Guihua Temple.
translations.idiomatic: At the Jinzhijiang the elephants panicked and trampled their own ranks; the rebel line shattered, the Qing forces pressed home, and the enemy fled in rout. The army then encamped east of the city at Guihua Temple.

sentences.zh: 九月，趙良棟師自四川至，遂合圍。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Zhao Liangdong's army arrived from Sichuan and the siege was complete.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Zhao Liangdong marched in from Sichuan and the encirclement was closed.

sentences.zh: 賚塔軍銀錠山，運砲至，晝夜番攻，世璠將餘從龍降。

translations.literal: Laita's army took Yinding Mountain; cannon were brought up and day and night assaults followed in rotation; Shifan's general Yu Conglong surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Laita seized Yinding Mountain, brought up artillery, and hammered the walls day and night in relays; Shifan's general Yu Conglong came over.

sentences.zh: 诇知糧將罄，人相食，與諸將環而攻之。

translations.literal: Scouts reported that grain was nearly exhausted and men were eating one another; with the generals he surrounded the city and pressed the attack.
translations.idiomatic: Intelligence showed the garrison was starving and men were eating one another; Laita and his generals ringed the city and pressed the assault.

sentences.zh: 世璠眾內亂，欲擒世璠以降，世璠自殺。

translations.literal: Shifan's followers fell into internal strife and wished to seize Shifan to surrender; Shifan killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Shifan's own men turned on one another, plotting to hand him over; Shifan took his own life.

sentences.zh: 其將夏國相奔廣南，胡國柱奔雲龍州。

translations.literal: His generals Xia Guoxiang fled to Guangnan and Hu Guozhu to Yunlong prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His generals Xia Guoxiang fled toward Guangnan and Hu Guozhu toward Yunlong.

sentences.zh: 遣諸將李國樑、希福等追襲之，擒國相，國柱自縊死。

translations.literal: He sent the generals Li Guoliang, Xifu, and others in pursuit; Guoxiang was captured and Guozhu hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Li Guoliang, Xifu, and others in pursuit; Guoxiang was taken alive and Guozhu hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 雲南大定。

translations.literal: Yunnan was wholly pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan was fully pacified.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，凱旋，上率群臣郊勞盧溝橋西，行抱見禮。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he returned in triumph; the emperor led the court in suburban honors west of the Lugou Bridge and performed the embrace-and-audience rite.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he returned in triumph; the emperor led the court in suburban honors west of the Lugou Bridge and received him with the embrace-and-audience ceremony.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，以隱匿之信籓下入官婦女，下所司集質。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, for concealing palace women taken from Zhixin's princely establishment, the case was sent to the relevant offices for joint examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he was accused of concealing palace women seized from Shang Zhixin's household; the matter was referred to the appropriate offices for investigation.

sentences.zh: 上諭賚塔有大功，勿以細事加罪。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed that Laita had great merit and was not to be punished for minor matters.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ruled that Laita's great services outweighed petty faults and that he was not to be punished on that account.

sentences.zh: 禮部議請奪官治罪，詔改降級罰俸。

translations.literal: The Board of Rites proposed stripping his rank and punishing him; an edict instead reduced his grade and fined his salary.
translations.idiomatic: The Board of Rites recommended dismissal and punishment; the emperor commuted the sentence to demotion and forfeiture of salary.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，卒，諡襄毅。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he died and was given the posthumous title Xiangyi.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-third year and was posthumously titled Xiangyi.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，追授一等阿思哈尼哈番。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was posthumously granted first-class commandant-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he was posthumously raised to first-class commandant-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 子費葉楞，襲。

translations.literal: His son Feiyeleng succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Feiyeleng inherited the rank.

sentences.zh: 雍正五年，世宗命追封一等公，令其孫博爾屯襲。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongzheng the Shizong emperor ordered posthumous enfeoffment as first-class duke and had his grandson Bo'ertun succeed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yongzheng the Yongzheng emperor posthumously enfeoffed him as first-class duke and had his grandson Bo'ertun inherit.

sentences.zh: 並諭：「賚塔克雲南，功績懋著。

translations.literal: An edict also stated: "Laita's capture of Yunnan was a service of outstanding merit.
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: "In taking Yunnan, Laita rendered outstanding service.

sentences.zh: 當日因其功過相掩，未予優封，欲使立功之臣，咸知儆惕收斂，不可恃功驕肆。

translations.literal: At the time, because merit and fault offset each other, no exceptional enfeoffment was granted, so that ministers who had won merit might all know to be wary and restrained and not rely on merit to grow arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: At the time his faults offset his merit, so no exceptional reward was given—so that men who had earned glory would learn caution and restraint and not grow arrogant on their achievements.

sentences.zh: 今事歷多年，後人已知鑑戒。

translations.literal: Now many years have passed and later men already know the lesson.
translations.idiomatic: Many years have passed since then, and later generations have taken the lesson to heart.

sentences.zh: 用特追封，示眷念舊臣。

translations.literal: Therefore a special posthumous enfeoffment is granted to show favor toward a former minister.
translations.idiomatic: A special posthumous enfeoffment is therefore granted to show remembrance of a faithful servant of old.

sentences.zh: 」九年，定公號曰褒績。

translations.literal: " In the ninth year the ducal title was fixed as Baoji.
translations.idiomatic: " In the ninth year his ducal designation was fixed as Baoji.

sentences.zh: 穆佔，納喇氏，滿洲正黃旗人，南楮子也。

translations.literal: Muzhan, of the Nara clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner and a son of Nanchu.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhan, of the Nara clan, belonged to the Plain Yellow Banner and was a son of Nanchu.

sentences.zh: 南楮事具楊吉砮傳。

translations.literal: Nanchu's career is given in full in the biography of Yangginu.
translations.idiomatic: Nanchu's career is recorded in the biography of Yangginu.

sentences.zh: 穆佔初任侍衛，兼牛錄額真。

translations.literal: Muzhan first served as guard and also held company command.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhan began as an imperial guard and also served as company commander.

sentences.zh: 順治十六年，署噶布什賢章京。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Shunzhi he acted as gabushan zhangjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Shunzhi he served as acting gabushan commander.

sentences.zh: 從都統卓洛等駐防雲南，平元江土司有功，予三等阿達哈哈番，擢本旗梅勒額真。

translations.literal: Following Lieutenant-general Zhuoluo and others he was garrisoned in Yunnan; pacifying the Yuanjiang chieftain he had merit, was granted third-class commandant, and was promoted banner vice-commander of his own banner.
translations.idiomatic: He garrisoned Yunnan under Lieutenant-general Zhuoluo and distinguished himself in pacifying the Yuanjiang chieftain; he was granted third-class commandant and made vice-commander of his banner.

sentences.zh: 康熙十二年冬，吳三桂反，命授赫葉安西將軍，道陝西入四川進討，以穆佔署前鋒統領，參贊軍務。

translations.literal: In the winter of the twelfth year of Kangxi Wu Sangui rebelled; Heyeh was appointed Pacification General of Anxi to enter Sichuan by way of Shaanxi, and Muzhan was made acting vanguard commander to assist in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the twelfth year of Kangxi, when Wu Sangui rebelled, Heyeh was named Pacification General of Anxi to advance into Sichuan through Shaanxi, with Muzhan as acting vanguard commander on his staff.

sentences.zh: 十三年二月，師至陝西，時四川巡撫羅森、提督鄭蛟麟皆附賊，總兵譚弘亦叛據陽平關。

translations.literal: In the second month of the thirteenth year the army reached Shaanxi; at that time the Sichuan governor Luo Sen and provincial military commissioner Zheng Jiaolin had both joined the rebels, and Regional Commander Tan Hong also rebelled and held Yangping Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the thirteenth year the army reached Shaanxi. Sichuan governor Luo Sen and military commissioner Zheng Jiaolin had gone over to the rebels, and Regional Commander Tan Hong held Yangping Pass in revolt.

sentences.zh: 穆佔與西安將軍瓦爾喀率兵先驅，戰野狐嶺，敗之，克陽平關。

translations.literal: Muzhan and the Xi'an general Warka led troops as vanguard, fought at Yehuling, defeated the enemy, and took Yangping Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhan and Xi'an general Warka led the vanguard, routed the rebels at Yehuling, and seized Yangping Pass.

sentences.zh: 總兵吳之茂叛據保寧，穆佔進與戰，屢擊敗之。

translations.literal: Regional Commander Wu Zhimao rebelled and held Baoning; Muzhan advanced and fought him, repeatedly defeating him.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Wu Zhimao rebelled and held Baoning; Muzhan advanced against him and defeated him again and again.

sentences.zh: 旋以賊阻餉道，引還漢中。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, because the rebels blocked the supply route, he withdrew to Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels cut his supply line he drew back to Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 提督王輔臣叛寧羌，與之茂、弘相應。

translations.literal: Provincial military commissioner Wang Fuchen rebelled at Ningqiang and acted in concert with Zhimao and Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Military commissioner Wang Fuchen rose at Ningqiang in concert with Zhimao and Tan Hong.

sentences.zh: 穆佔從大將軍貝勒洞鄂還西安。

translations.literal: Muzhan followed Grand General Prince Tonge back to Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhan withdrew to Xi'an with Grand General Prince Tonge.

sentences.zh: 十四年，詔趣洞鄂討輔臣，而以穆佔代赫葉為安西將軍，率師並進。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year an edict urged Tonge to suppress Fuchen, and Muzhan replaced Heyeh as Pacification General of Anxi and led the armies forward together.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year the court pressed Tonge to crush Fuchen and named Muzhan Pacification General of Anxi in Heyeh's place; he led the armies forward in concert.

sentences.zh: 輔臣將高鼎屯隴州河岸，迎戰，與達理善擊卻之。

translations.literal: Fuchen's general Gao Ding encamped on the Longzhou riverbank to give battle; with Dalishan he drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: Fuchen's general Gao Ding held the Longzhou riverbank to meet them; Muzhan and Dalishan beat him back.

sentences.zh: 趨秦州，圍合，輔臣將陳萬策以城降。

translations.literal: Pressing on to Qinzhou, the siege closed, and Fuchen's general Chen Wance surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed on to Qinzhou, closed the siege, and Fuchen's general Chen Wance surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 穆佔复助提督張勇攻下鞏昌，還會諸軍徵平涼。

translations.literal: Muzhan again assisted military commissioner Zhang Yong in taking Gongchang, then rejoined the armies in the campaign against Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhan then helped military commissioner Zhang Yong take Gongchang and rejoined the main force for the campaign against Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 十五年，上遣圖海代洞鄂為大將軍，輔臣降。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year the emperor sent Tu Hai to replace Tonge as grand general, and Fuchen surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year the emperor replaced Tonge with Tu Hai as grand general, and Fuchen submitted.

sentences.zh: 穆佔分剿餘寇，以次復西河、清水、成、禮諸縣。

translations.literal: Muzhan separately routed the remaining rebels and, in succession, recovered Xihe, Qingshui, Cheng, Li, and the other counties.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhan mopped up the remaining rebels and, one after another, restored Xihe, Qingshui, Cheng, Li, and the neighboring counties.

sentences.zh: 輔臣將周養民等以慶陽降。

translations.literal: Fuchen's generals Zhou Yangmin and others surrendered at Qingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Fuchen's commanders Zhou Yangmin and others came over at Qingyang.

sentences.zh: 九月，詔入覲，進秩視都統，佩征南將軍印，統陝西、河南諸軍赴湖廣，討三桂，諸將塔勒岱、鄂克遜從。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he was summoned to audience, advanced in rank to the equivalent of lieutenant-general, invested with the seal of General Who Campaigns South, and placed in command of the armies of Shaanxi and Henan to proceed to Huguang against Wu Sangui; the generals Taledai and Ekexun followed him.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he was called to court, raised to lieutenant-general's rank, given the seal of General Who Campaigns South, and ordered to lead the Shaanxi and Henan forces into Huguang against Wu Sangui, with Taledai and Ekexun under his command.

sentences.zh: 十六年正月，至荊州。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixteenth year he reached Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the sixteenth year he arrived at Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 時大將軍順承郡王勒克德渾守荊州，貝勒尚善圍岳州，安親王岳樂圍長沙，簡親王喇布守吉安。

translations.literal: At that time Grand General Prince Shuncheng Lekedehun garrisoned Jingzhou; Prince Beile Shangshan besieged Yuezhou; Prince An Yuele besieged Changsha; and Prince Jian Labu garrisoned Ji'an.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Prince Shuncheng Lekedehun held Jingzhou; Prince Beile Shangshan had Yuezhou under siege; Prince An Yuele was investing Changsha; and Prince Jian Labu guarded Ji'an.

sentences.zh: 上命穆佔助攻長沙，軍至，屯阿彌嶺。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Muzhan to assist in the attack on Changsha; when the army arrived it encamped at Amiling.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Muzhan to join the assault on Changsha, and when his troops arrived they encamped at Amiling.

sentences.zh: 三桂初欲自松滋渡江，進攻荊州，相持數年不得逞。

translations.literal: Wu Sangui had at first intended to cross the river at Songzi and advance against Jingzhou, but after several years of stalemate he had been unable to carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui had first planned to cross at Songzi and strike Jingzhou, yet years of deadlock had denied him any opening.

sentences.zh: 聞長沙有新軍至，亟自松滋還援，屯隔江岳麓山。

translations.literal: Hearing that new troops had reached Changsha, he hurried back from Songzi to relieve the city and encamped on Yuelu Mountain across the river.
translations.idiomatic: When word came that fresh troops had reached Changsha, he rushed back from Songzi to relieve the city and made camp on Yuelu Mountain on the far bank.

sentences.zh: 遣其將馬寶等屯城外，掘重壕，布鐵蒺藜，列象陣以守；

translations.literal: He dispatched his generals Ma Bao and others to encamp outside the city walls, dig deep moats, deploy iron caltrops, and array elephant formations to hold the place.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Ma Bao and other commanders to hold positions outside the walls, cut deep trenches, strew iron caltrops, and form elephant lines for the defense.

sentences.zh: 而自從常德進，為穆佔所敗，走衡州。

translations.literal: He himself, however, advanced from Changde and was defeated by Muzhan, fleeing to Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then marched out from Changde in person, was beaten by Muzhan, and fled to Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 上命穆佔移兵會簡親王取衡州。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Muzhan to shift his forces and join Prince Jian in taking Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Muzhan to move his army and unite with Prince Jian to seize Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 十月，克茶陵，复攸、安仁、酃、永寧諸縣。

translations.literal: In the tenth month they captured Chaling and recovered You, Anren, Ling, Yongning, and the other counties.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month they took Chaling and restored You, Anren, Ling, Yongning, and the surrounding counties.

sentences.zh: 十七年春，克郴州，傍縣並下。

translations.literal: In the spring of the seventeenth year they captured Chenzhou, and the neighboring counties all fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the seventeenth year they seized Chenzhou, and the counties around it fell in turn.

sentences.zh: 穆佔守郴州，以都統宜理布守永興。

translations.literal: Muzhan garrisoned Chenzhou and left Lieutenant-general Yilibu to hold Yongxing.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhan held Chenzhou and posted Lieutenant-general Yilibu at Yongxing.

sentences.zh: 三桂欲通粵東道，與尚之信、孫延齡軍合，遣其將馬寶、胡國柱等悉銳攻永興。

translations.literal: Wu Sangui wished to open a route through eastern Guangdong to join the armies of Shang Zhixin and Sun Yanling, and sent his generals Ma Bao, Hu Guozhu, and others with all their elite forces to attack Yongxing.
translations.idiomatic: Seeking a corridor into eastern Guangdong to link with the armies of Shang Zhixin and Sun Yanling, Wu Sangui sent Ma Bao, Hu Guozhu, and other commanders with every crack unit against Yongxing.

sentences.zh: 穆佔遣哈克三、碩岱來援。

translations.literal: Muzhan dispatched Hakasan and Shuodai to reinforce.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhan sent Hakasan and Shuodai to the relief.

sentences.zh: 時喇布尚駐吉安，穆佔請旨趣進徵。

translations.literal: At that time Labu was still stationed at Ji'an, and Muzhan requested imperial orders to urge him forward on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Labu was still at Ji'an, and Muzhan asked the throne to press him into the field.

sentences.zh: 六月，宜理布、哈克三戰死。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Yilibu and Hakasan died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Yilibu and Hakasan were killed in action.

sentences.zh: 碩岱入城守，喇布遣薩克察來援，牒穆佔請益兵。

translations.literal: Shuodai entered the city to hold it; Labu sent Sakicha to reinforce and dispatched a note to Muzhan requesting additional troops.
translations.idiomatic: Shuodai withdrew into the city to hold it; Labu sent Sakicha to reinforce and wrote Muzhan asking for more men.

sentences.zh: 穆佔謂永興軍事簡親王主之。

translations.literal: Muzhan replied that military affairs at Yongxing were under Prince Jian's authority.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhan answered that Prince Jian had charge of operations at Yongxing.

sentences.zh: 喇布以聞，上責穆佔謬戾。

translations.literal: Labu reported this to the throne, and the emperor rebuked Muzhan for perversity.
translations.idiomatic: Labu reported the exchange, and the emperor censured Muzhan for obstinacy.

sentences.zh: 寶、國柱攻永興，二十餘日不下，聞三桂死，乃引還衡州。

translations.literal: Bao and Guozhu besieged Yongxing for more than twenty days without taking it; on hearing that Wu Sangui had died, they withdrew to Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Bao and Hu Guozhu hammered Yongxing for more than twenty days without success; when news came of Wu Sangui's death they pulled back to Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 穆佔率布舒庫等追擊，敗之耒陽。

translations.literal: Muzhan led Bushuku and others in pursuit and defeated them at Leiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhan pursued with Bushuku and others and routed them at Leiyang.

sentences.zh: 十八年，三桂將吳國貴為他將所䠞，遁永州，穆佔追剿，克之，道州、常寧、新田、永明、江華、東安皆下。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Wu Sangui's general Wu Guogui was ousted by another commander and fled to Yongzhou; Muzhan pursued and destroyed him, took the city, and Daozhou, Changning, Xintian, Yongming, Jianghua, and Dong'an all fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year Wu Sangui's general Wu Guogui was overthrown by a fellow officer and fled to Yongzhou; Muzhan ran him down, captured the city, and brought Daozhou, Changning, Xintian, Yongming, Jianghua, and Dong'an under control.

sentences.zh: 師入廣西境，克全州、灌陽、興安、恭城。

translations.literal: The army entered Guangxi and captured Quanzhou, Guanyang, Xing'an, and Gongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: The column crossed into Guangxi and took Quanzhou, Guanyang, Xing'an, and Gongcheng.

sentences.zh: 詔還定湖南，進克新寧。

translations.literal: An edict ordered them to return and secure Hunan; they advanced and captured Xinning.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered them back to settle Hunan; they pushed on and seized Xinning.

sentences.zh: 三桂將郭壯圖等擁三桂孫世璠據貴州。

translations.literal: Wu Sangui's generals Guo Zhuangtu and others had Wu Sangui's grandson Wu Shifan hold Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui's generals Guo Zhuangtu and others installed Wu Sangui's grandson Wu Shifan in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 十一月，上命貝子彰泰為定遠平寇大將軍，規定雲、貴，穆佔參贊軍務。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the emperor appointed Imperial Prince Zhangtai Grand General for Pacifying Distant Rebels to conquer Yunnan and Guizhou, with Muzhan assisting in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the emperor named Imperial Prince Zhangtai Grand General for Pacifying Distant Rebels to recover Yunnan and Guizhou, with Muzhan on his staff.

sentences.zh: 十九年二月，复沅州。

translations.literal: In the second month of the nineteenth year they recovered Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the nineteenth year Yuanzhou was restored.

sentences.zh: 十月，克鎮遠，並定偏橋、興隆二衛。

translations.literal: In the tenth month they captured Zhenyuan and secured the two garrisons of Pianqiao and Xinglong.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month they took Zhenyuan and brought the Pianqiao and Xinglong garrisons to heel.

sentences.zh: 進克平越，下貴陽。

translations.literal: They advanced, captured Pingyue, and took Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed forward, seized Pingyue, and entered Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 世璠奔雲南。

translations.literal: Wu Shifan fled to Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shifan fled into Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 十一月，克遵義、安順、石阡、都勻、思南諸府。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month they captured the prefectures of Zunyi, Anshun, Shiqian, Duyun, and Sinan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month they recovered the prefectures of Zunyi, Anshun, Shiqian, Duyun, and Sinan.

sentences.zh: 二十年正月，世璠將夏國相、高起隆、王會、楊應選等擁眾二萬拒戰，屯平遠西南山。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twentieth year Wu Shifan's generals Xia Guoxiang, Gao Qilong, Wang Hui, Yang Yingxuan, and others mustered twenty thousand men to resist, encamping on the southwest mountain at Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twentieth year Wu Shifan's commanders Xia Guoxiang, Gao Qilong, Wang Hui, Yang Yingxuan, and others gathered twenty thousand men to give battle and camped on the mountain southwest of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 穆佔與提督趙賴督諸軍奮擊，起隆等敗竄，會降，遂復平遠。

translations.literal: Muzhan, together with provincial military commissioner Zhao Lai, directed the armies in fierce assault; Qilong and the others were defeated and fled in disarray, Hui surrendered, and Pingyuan was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhan and provincial military commissioner Zhao Lai led a furious attack; Gao Qilong and his fellows broke and scattered, Wang Hui submitted, and Pingyuan was retaken.

sentences.zh: 分遣諸將莽奕祿等逐賊，復大定，應選亦降。

translations.literal: He dispatched the generals Mang Yilu and others to pursue the rebels, recovered Dading, and Yingxuan also surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Mang Yilu and other commanders after the fugitives, restored Dading, and Yang Yingxuan came over as well.

sentences.zh: 遂入雲南，與廣西軍會，壁歸化寺。

translations.literal: They then entered Yunnan, joined the Guangxi army, and encamped at Guihua Temple.
translations.idiomatic: They marched into Yunnan, united with the Guangxi force, and made camp at Guihua Temple.

sentences.zh: 壯圖出兵重關，列象陣犯我軍。

translations.literal: Zhuangtu led troops out through the fortified pass, arrayed elephant formations, and assaulted our army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangtu sallied through the heavy pass with war elephants drawn up and struck the Qing line.

sentences.zh: 賚塔等縱兵夾擊，穆佔戰尤力，象陣亂，反踐其軍。

translations.literal: Laita and the others unleashed their forces in a pincer attack; Muzhan fought with especial vigor; the elephant formations fell into chaos and trampled their own troops.
translations.idiomatic: Laita and his officers closed from both sides while Muzhan fought hardest of all; the elephants panicked, turned on their own ranks, and trampled them down.

sentences.zh: 諸軍乘之，壯圖斂兵，止存二十七人，奔入城。

translations.literal: The armies pressed the advantage; Zhuangtu gathered in his troops, retaining only twenty-seven men, and fled into the city.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing forces pressed the rout; Zhuangtu pulled his men in with only twenty-seven left and bolted back into the city.

sentences.zh: 九月，四川軍至，總督蔡毓榮破重關，穆佔亦奪玉皇閣，猛攻東西寺。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the Sichuan army arrived; Governor-General Cai Yurong broke through the fortified pass, and Muzhan also seized Yuhuang Pavilion and fiercely assaulted the Eastern and Western Temples.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the Sichuan column arrived; Governor-General Cai Yurong forced the heavy pass while Muzhan took Yuhuang Pavilion and hammered the Eastern and Western Temples.

sentences.zh: 世璠、壯圖皆自殺。

translations.literal: Wu Shifan and Zhuangtu both committed suicide.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shifan and Zhuangtu both took their own lives.

sentences.zh: 穆佔入城，撫餘眾，籍逆產以聞。

translations.literal: Muzhan entered the city, pacified the remaining populace, and registered rebel property to report to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhan entered the city, quieted the people who remained, inventoried rebel holdings, and memorialized the court.

sentences.zh: 師還，授正黃旗蒙古都統、議政大臣。

translations.literal: When the army returned he was appointed Mongol lieutenant-general of the Plain Yellow Banner and grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return he was made Mongol lieutenant-general of the Plain Yellow Banner and a grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，追論徵保寧時奏軍事不實，徵平涼時不臨陣指揮，及不救永興，罪當絞，籍沒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year a retrospective inquiry found that in the campaign at Baoning he had reported military affairs falsely, that at Pingliang he had not personally commanded from the battlefield, and that he had failed to relieve Yongxing; his crime merited strangulation and confiscation of property.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year a posthumous review held that he had filed false battle reports at Baoning, had not led from the front at Pingliang, and had failed to save Yongxing; the penalty was death by strangulation and confiscation of his estate.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「穆佔固有罪，但其戰績多至二百六十處，此所議稍過。

translations.literal: The emperor decreed: "Muzhan is indeed guilty, but his battle record extends to more than two hundred and sixty engagements—this judgment goes somewhat too far.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Muzhan is guilty, yet his record runs to more than two hundred and sixty engagements—the proposed sentence is too harsh."

sentences.zh: 」命覆議，乃請奪官、削世職、沒妻子入內務府，上命但奪官，餘悉寬之。

translations.literal: " He ordered a re-deliberation; they then requested stripping of rank, removal of the hereditary office, and enrollment of wife and children in the Imperial Household Department; the emperor ordered only the stripping of rank and pardoned the rest.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the case reopened; the reviewers then asked that he be stripped of office, lose his hereditary post, and have wife and children enrolled in the Imperial Household Department, but the emperor commanded that only his rank be taken and the rest be remitted.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died.

sentences.zh: 莽依圖，兆佳氏，滿洲鑲白旗人。

translations.literal: Mangyitu, of the Zhaojia clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Mangyitu, of the Zhaojia clan, belonged to the Bordered White Banner.

sentences.zh: 父武達禪，崇德中從伐明，攻任丘、濟陽，並先登，賜號「巴圖魯」，予牛錄章京世職。

translations.literal: His father was Wudachan. During the Chongde reign he followed the campaign against Ming, attacked Renqiu and Jiyang, and was first to scale the walls at both; he was granted the title "baturu" and given the hereditary office of company commander.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wudachan had campaigned against Ming in the Chongde era, stormed Renqiu and Jiyang, and been first over the walls at both places; for this he received the title baturu and a hereditary company commandership.

sentences.zh: 既入關，授太原城守尉。

translations.literal: After entering the pass, he was appointed garrison commander of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Once the army had crossed into China proper, he was made garrison commander of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 莽依圖襲職，進三等阿達哈哈番。

translations.literal: Mangyitu inherited the office and was advanced to third-class commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Mangyitu succeeded to the family post and was raised to third-class commandant.

sentences.zh: 順治十五年，從征南將軍卓卜特下貴州，自都勻次盤江，破明將李定國。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Shunzhi he followed Pacification General of the South Zhuobote into Guizhou; from Duyun he halted at Panjiang and defeated the Ming general Li Dingguo.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Shunzhi he marched under Pacification General of the South Zhuobote into Guizhou, advanced from Duyun to the Pan River, and routed the Ming general Li Dingguo.

sentences.zh: 移師定雲南。

translations.literal: The army shifted to pacify Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: The army then turned to pacify Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 康熙二年，李自成餘黨李來亨等據湖北茅麓山，未下，從靖西將軍穆里瑪攻克之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kangxi, Li Laiheng and other remnant followers of Li Zicheng held Maolu Mountain in Hubei and could not be reduced; Mangyitu followed Pacification General of the West Murima and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kangxi, Li Laiheng and other survivors of Li Zicheng held out on Maolu Mountain in Hubei; Mangyitu served under Pacification General of the West Murima and took the position.

sentences.zh: 凱旋，授江寧協領。

translations.literal: Returning in triumph, he was appointed assistant commander at Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: After the victorious return he was named assistant commander at Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 十三年，吳三桂陷湖南，復從鎮南將軍尼雅翰攻岳州，砲擊寇艦，敗之七里橋。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Wu Sangui took Hunan; Mangyitu again followed Pacification General of the South Nyahha to attack Yuezhou, bombarded the rebel ships, and defeated them at Qiliqiao.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, when Wu Sangui overran Hunan, Mangyitu again served under Pacification General of the South Nyahha at the siege of Yuezhou, shelled the rebel fleet, and drove them off at Qiliqiao.

sentences.zh: 十四年，三桂構廣西總兵馬雄叛，廣東十府失其四。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Wu Sangui induced the Guangxi provincial commander Ma Xiong to rebel, and four of Guangdong's ten prefectures were lost.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year Wu Sangui turned the Guangxi provincial commander Ma Xiong, and four of Guangdong's ten prefectures fell to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 尚可喜請兵，上命尼雅翰率師赴廣東，以莽依圖署副都統，駐肇慶。

translations.literal: Shang Kexi requested troops; the emperor ordered Nyahha to lead an army to Guangdong, with Mangyitu acting as deputy lieutenant-general stationed at Zhaoqing.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Kexi appealed for reinforcements, and the emperor sent Nyahha south into Guangdong with Mangyitu as acting deputy lieutenant-general at Zhaoqing.

sentences.zh: 甫至，而可喜子之信已叛應三桂。

translations.literal: Hardly had they arrived when Kexi's son Zhixin had already rebelled in answer to Wu Sangui.
translations.idiomatic: They had scarcely arrived when Shang Kexi's son Zhixin had already gone over to Wu Sangui.

sentences.zh: 十五年，三桂將範齊韓等偪肇慶，莽依圖潰圍出，且戰且走，還駐江西。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Wu Sangui's generals Fan Qihan and others pressed Zhaoqing; Mangyitu broke out of the encirclement, fighting as he withdrew, and fell back to Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year Fan Qihan and other Wu Sangui generals closed on Zhaoqing; Mangyitu cut his way out, fighting a running withdrawal, and regrouped in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 聞三桂將黃士標等攻信豐，亟率師赴援，遣奇兵出其背，與城兵衷擊之，賊大潰，遂會鎮南將軍覺羅舒恕解南康圍。

translations.literal: Hearing that Wu Sangui's generals Huang Shibiao and others were attacking Xinfeng, he urgently led troops to their relief, sent a flanking force behind them, and with the garrison struck them from both sides; the rebels were routed, and he then joined Pacification General of the South Shuxu to lift the siege of Nankang.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned that Huang Shibiao and other Wu Sangui generals were besieging Xinfeng, he rushed to relieve the city, sent a detachment to take the enemy in the rear, and with the garrison crushed them in a pincer; the rebels broke and fled, and he joined Pacification General of the South Shuxu in raising the siege of Nankang.

sentences.zh: 十六年三月，上命舒恕留兵守贛州，而授莽依圖署江寧副都統，代舒恕佩鎮南將軍印，帥師規复廣東，以額赫訥、穆成額參贊軍事。

translations.literal: In the third month of the sixteenth year the emperor ordered Shuxu to leave troops to hold Ganzhou, appointed Mangyitu acting deputy lieutenant-general at Jiangning, and had him replace Shuxu in bearing the seal of Pacification General of the South and lead an army to recover Guangdong, with Ehene and Muchenge assisting in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the sixteenth year the emperor left Shuxu to garrison Ganzhou, made Mangyitu acting deputy lieutenant-general at Jiangning, and transferred to him the seal of Pacification General of the South so that he might lead the campaign to recover Guangdong, with Ehene and Muchenge on his staff.

sentences.zh: 自南康進南安，再進南雄，三桂所遣守將皆出降，之信亦率籓屬歸順。

translations.literal: Advancing from Nankang to Nan'an and then to Nanxiong, every garrison commander Wu Sangui had posted came out to surrender, and Zhixin also led his household and retainers back to allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: From Nankang he pushed on to Nan'an and then Nanxiong; Wu Sangui's garrison commanders surrendered one after another, and Zhixin too submitted with his household and followers.

sentences.zh: 莽依圖遂踰嶺進韶州，韶居五嶺脊，為贛、粵咽喉，賊所必爭。

translations.literal: Mangyitu then crossed the ridge and entered Shaozhou. Shaozhou sits on the spine of the Five Ridges and is the throat between Jiangxi and Guangdong—a place the rebels were bound to contest.
translations.idiomatic: Mangyitu crossed the mountains into Shaozhou, a city on the backbone of the Five Ridges and the hinge between Jiangxi and Guangdong—ground no rebel army could afford to yield.

sentences.zh: 莽依圖以城北當敵衝，厚增土牆，夜則縋卒出城濬壕通水，並分兵斷廣州餉道。

translations.literal: Mangyitu faced the north of the city toward the enemy's main thrust, greatly thickened the earthen walls, and at night lowered men by rope to dredge the moat and connect it to water; he also detached troops to cut Guangzhou's supply route.
translations.idiomatic: Mangyitu turned the city's northern face to the enemy's line of attack and raised the earthen ramparts higher; by night he lowered men over the walls to dredge the moat and link it to open water, and sent detachments to sever Guangzhou's supply lines.

sentences.zh: 三桂將胡國柱、馬寶以萬餘人攻城，莽依圖屢擊卻之；

translations.literal: Wu Sangui's generals Hu Guozhu and Ma Bao attacked the city with more than ten thousand men, and Mangyitu repeatedly struck and drove them back;
translations.idiomatic: Hu Guozhu and Ma Bao, Wu Sangui's generals, assaulted the city with more than ten thousand men, and Mangyitu beat them back again and again;

sentences.zh: 乃扼河西斷我水運，又壁蓮花山發砲，女牆悉壞。

translations.literal: they then held the west of the river and cut off our water transport, fortified on Lianhua Mountain to fire cannon, and destroyed the parapets entirely.
translations.idiomatic: then they seized the west bank, choked off river supply, and from fortified positions on Lianhua Mountain shelled the walls until the parapets were shattered.

sentences.zh: 會江寧將軍額楚赴援，莽依圖出城兵夾擊，破四壘，逐北至帽峰山，夜戰，大敗之。

translations.literal: When Jiangning General Echu arrived to reinforce him, Mangyitu led the garrison in a pincer attack, broke four camps, pursued the enemy north to Maofeng Mountain, fought through the night, and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Echu, the Jiangning general, came up with reinforcements; Mangyitu sallied forth and caught the enemy between two forces, overran four camps, pursued them to Maofeng Mountain, and after fighting through the night broke them completely.

sentences.zh: 河西賊亦引去，餉運始通。

translations.literal: The rebels west of the river also withdrew, and supply transport was restored at last.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy west of the river pulled back as well, and the supply route was open again.

sentences.zh: 莽依圖督軍追擊，破敵風門澳，斬二千餘級。

translations.literal: Mangyitu directed the army in pursuit, defeated the enemy at Fengmen'ao, and took more than two thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Mangyitu pressed the pursuit, routed the enemy at Fengmen'ao, and took more than two thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 下樂昌、仁化諸縣，乃還駐韶州。

translations.literal: He reduced Lechang, Renhua, and other counties, then returned to garrison Shaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: After taking Lechang, Renhua, and the surrounding counties, he returned to hold Shaozhou.

sentences.zh: 時傅弘烈佩撫蠻滅寇將軍印，巡撫廣西，所將義兵五千人。

translations.literal: At that time Fu Honglie bore the seal of General for Pacifying Barbarians and Destroying Bandits as governor of Guangxi, leading five thousand volunteer troops.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Fu Honglie, governor of Guangxi, held the seal of General for Pacifying Barbarians and Destroying Bandits and commanded five thousand militia.

sentences.zh: 莽依圖慮其力不支，遣副都統額赫訥將兵八千赴梧州佐弘烈，而之信不為具舟，師久不集。

translations.literal: Mangyitu feared his force was too weak, and dispatched Deputy Lieutenant-General Ehene with eight thousand men to Wuzhou to assist Honglie; but Zhixin failed to furnish boats, and the army long failed to assemble.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Fu Honglie was overmatched, Mangyitu sent Deputy Lieutenant-General Ehene with eight thousand men to Wuzhou to support him; Zhixin, however, would not provide transport, and the troops lingered for weeks without gathering.

sentences.zh: 十七年二月，莽依圖至平樂，圍城，寇水陸拒戰，引還中山鎮，與弘烈互奏糾，上兩釋之。

translations.literal: In the second month of the seventeenth year Mangyitu reached Pingle and besieged the city; the bandits resisted by land and water, and he withdrew to Zhongshan Town. He and Honglie mutually memorialized accusations against each other, and the emperor released them both from blame.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the seventeenth year Mangyitu invested Pingle, but the rebels held him off on land and water and he fell back to Zhongshan Town; he and Fu Honglie then filed rival accusations, and the emperor dismissed the charges against both men.

sentences.zh: 莽依圖復還梧州，引咎請罷將軍，上切責之，命留任圖功贖罪。

translations.literal: Mangyitu returned again to Wuzhou, took blame upon himself, and asked to be relieved of the generalship; the emperor sharply rebuked him and ordered him to remain in office and win merit to atone for his fault.
translations.idiomatic: Mangyitu withdrew to Wuzhou, accepted responsibility, and asked to surrender his command; the emperor rebuked him sternly and told him to keep his post and redeem himself with victories.

sentences.zh: 十八年春，三桂從孫世琮犯梧州，莽依圖與弘烈謀合諸軍分佈水陸，與戰，賊敗去，遂復桂林。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eighteenth year Wu Sangui's grand-nephew Shizong attacked Wuzhou; Mangyitu and Honglie planned to combine their armies on land and water, gave battle, drove the bandits off, and recovered Guilin.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the eighteenth year Wu Sangui's grand-nephew Shizong struck at Wuzhou; Mangyitu and Fu Honglie united their forces on land and water, defeated the rebels, and retook Guilin.

sentences.zh: 語具弘烈傳。

translations.literal: The full account is given in Honglie's biography.
translations.idiomatic: The fuller account appears in Fu Honglie's biography.

sentences.zh: 三桂將馬承廕以南寧來降，世琮自梧州敗歸，並力攻南寧。

translations.literal: Wu Sangui's general Ma Chengyin came over with Nanning; Shizong returned defeated from Wuzhou, and together they pressed the attack on Nanning.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui's general Ma Chengyin surrendered Nanning; Shizong, retreating from Wuzhou, joined him in a combined assault on the city.

sentences.zh: 城幾陷，莽依圖方臥病，聞警，督軍倍道赴援。

translations.literal: The city was near falling when Mangyitu, then bedridden with illness, heard the alarm, roused himself, and forced the army forward at double speed to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: Nanning was on the verge of collapse when Mangyitu, sick abed, heard the alarm, roused himself, and marched the army at forced pace to its rescue.

sentences.zh: 賊悉銳依山列鹿角拒戰，莽依圖使額楚、額赫訥引前鋒兵衝擊之，而自與舒恕麾大軍進，預遣兵潛出山後斷歸路，盡殪之。

translations.literal: The bandits brought up their best troops, lined abatis along the hills, and resisted; Mangyitu had Echu and Ehene lead the vanguard in a charge while he himself, with Shuxu, commanded the main army forward, having already sent men secretly around the mountain to cut off their retreat; the enemy were annihilated to the last man.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels massed their elite along the hills behind abatis; Mangyitu sent Echu and Ehene to smash the front while he and Shuxu led the main body forward, having already slipped troops around the mountain to seal the retreat—every man of the enemy force was killed.

sentences.zh: 世琮負重傷，以數十騎越山遁。

translations.literal: Shizong, gravely wounded, fled over the mountains with several dozen horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong, badly wounded, escaped over the mountains with only a few dozen riders.

sentences.zh: 南寧圍解。

translations.literal: The siege of Nanning was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: The siege of Nanning was raised.

sentences.zh: 命進取雲、貴，莽依圖以承廕雖降，心叵測，疏請暫駐南寧。

translations.literal: Ordered to advance and take Yunnan and Guizhou, Mangyitu, though Chengyin had surrendered, judged his intentions untrustworthy and memorialized asking to remain temporarily at Nanning.
translations.idiomatic: When orders came to push into Yunnan and Guizhou, Mangyitu—doubting Ma Chengyin despite his surrender—memorialized the throne asking to hold Nanning for the time being.

sentences.zh: 上命簡親王喇布鎮桂林，莽依圖俟都統希福軍至，合兵謀進取。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Prince Jian Labu to garrison Guilin; Mangyitu waited for Lieutenant-General Xifu's army to arrive so that their forces might be combined for the advance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor posted Prince Jian Labu at Guilin while Mangyitu waited for Lieutenant-General Xifu's column to arrive before planning the next advance.

sentences.zh: 十九年，授護軍統領。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was appointed commander of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he was made commander of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 承廕果以柳州复叛，弘烈遇害。

translations.literal: Chengyin did indeed rebel again from Liuzhou, and Honglie was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chengyin duly rose again from Liuzhou, and Fu Honglie lost his life.

sentences.zh: 莽依圖軍進次宜賓，承廕驅象陣迎戰，以勁弩射之，象返奔，賊陣亂，鐵騎乘之，遂大敗。

translations.literal: Mangyitu's army advanced and halted at Yibin; Chengyin drove an elephant formation to meet battle; strong crossbows were loosed at the elephants, they turned and fled, the bandit ranks broke, iron cavalry seized the moment, and a great defeat followed.
translations.idiomatic: Mangyitu's army halted at Yibin; Ma Chengyin sent an elephant corps against him, but volleys of heavy crossbow bolts sent the beasts stampeding back through their own lines; armored cavalry charged into the chaos and broke the enemy utterly.

sentences.zh: 承廕復以柳州降。

translations.literal: Chengyin again surrendered with Liuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Chengyin submitted once more, yielding Liuzhou.

sentences.zh: 莽依圖疾益深，八月，卒於軍。

translations.literal: Mangyitu's illness grew worse; in the eighth month he died in camp.
translations.idiomatic: Mangyitu's illness deepened, and in the eighth month he died in the field.

sentences.zh: 莽依圖母賢，嘗訓以不殺降，不掠民，莽依圖終身誦之，時稱「仁義將軍」。

translations.literal: Mangyitu's mother was a woman of virtue who had admonished him never to kill those who surrendered and never to plunder the people; Mangyitu repeated her words all his life, and men of the time called him the "Benevolent and Righteous General."
translations.idiomatic: Mangyitu's mother had been a woman of principle who taught him never to slaughter prisoners or prey on civilians; he lived by her words all his days, and his contemporaries named him the Benevolent and Righteous General.

sentences.zh: 既卒，南寧人繪其像祀之。

translations.literal: After his death the people of Nanning painted his portrait and worshipped him.
translations.idiomatic: After his death the people of Nanning painted his likeness and enshrined him in worship.

sentences.zh: 事平，朝議追論自平樂還梧州失律罪，當籍沒。

translations.literal: When the rebellion was pacified, the court reviewed his offense of breach of military discipline in returning from Pingle to Wuzhou and held that his property should be confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Once peace was restored, the court reopened the charge that he had violated military discipline by withdrawing from Pingle to Wuzhou and recommended confiscation of his estate.

sentences.zh: 上以莽依圖戰多，且不擾民，寬之，奪恩詔所加世職，以原授拜他喇布勒哈番兼拖沙喇哈番予其弟博和里。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Mangyitu had fought in many battles and had not harassed the people, showed leniency; he stripped the hereditary rank added by grace edict and granted the originally conferred ranks of deputy company commander and captain to his younger brother Boheli.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, weighing Mangyitu's long record in battle and his restraint toward civilians, was merciful: he removed the grace-edict hereditary rank but passed the original deputy company commandership and captaincy to Mangyitu's younger brother Boheli.

sentences.zh: 博和里曰：「兄平粵有功，上褒之，不可使吾子孫復襲此職。

translations.literal: Boheli said: "My elder brother pacified Guangdong with merit, and the emperor praised him; our descendants must not inherit this office again.
translations.idiomatic: Boheli said, "My brother earned his honors pacifying Guangdong, and the emperor himself commended him—our line ought not inherit this post again.

sentences.zh: 」乃撫其孫布瞻阿繼襲。

translations.literal: " He then had his nephew Buzhan'a succeed in inheritance.
translations.idiomatic: " So he placed his nephew Buzhan'a in succession instead.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，追諡襄壯。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong he was posthumously enfeoffed as Xiangzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianlong he received the posthumous name Xiangzhuang.

sentences.zh: 三桂初反，十三年正月，上授都統尼雅翰鎮南將軍，會師德州，道安慶至武昌。

translations.literal: When Wu Sangui first rebelled, in the first month of the thirteenth year the emperor appointed Lieutenant-General Nyahha Pacification General of the South; the army assembled at Dezhou and marched by way of Anqing to Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset of Wu Sangui's rebellion, in the first month of the thirteenth year the emperor named Lieutenant-General Nyahha Pacification General of the South; his forces gathered at Dezhou and advanced through Anqing to Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 尋命參贊軍務，攻岳州；

translations.literal: Soon after, he was ordered to assist in military affairs and attack Yuezhou;
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was ordered to serve on the staff and attack Yuezhou;

sentences.zh: 旋又命進取南康，克之；

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was again ordered to advance and take Nankang, and captured it;
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to push on and seize Nankang, which he took;

sentences.zh: 又擊破三桂將黃乃忠等於袁州。

translations.literal: Again he defeated Wu Sangui's generals Huang Naizhong and others at Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He again routed Wu Sangui's generals Huang Naizhong and others at Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 十五年五月，上命哈爾哈齊率江寧兵攻吉安，解尼雅翰鎮南將軍印授之；

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fifteenth year the emperor ordered Harhaqi to lead Jiangning troops against Ji'an, removed Nyahha's seal as Pacification General of the South, and conferred it upon him;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fifteenth year the emperor ordered Harhaqi to lead Jiangning forces against Ji'an, stripped Nyahha of the Pacification General of the South seal, and gave it to Harhaqi;

sentences.zh: 螺子山敗，改授覺羅舒恕。

translations.literal: After defeat at Luozi Mountain, it was instead conferred upon Aisin Gioro Shuxu.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat at Luozi Mountain, the seal passed instead to Aisin Gioro Shuxu.

sentences.zh: 覺羅舒恕，滿洲正白旗人，武功郡王禮敦曾孫。

translations.literal: Aisin Gioro Shuxu was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner and the great-grandson of Prince Kewu of Wugong, Lidun.
translations.idiomatic: Aisin Gioro Shuxu belonged to the Plain White Banner and was the great-grandson of Prince Kewu of Wugong, Lidun.

sentences.zh: 康熙八年，自一等侍衛授兵部督捕侍郎，調吏部。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Kangxi, from first-class bodyguard he was appointed vice-minister of War in charge of pursuit and arrest, then transferred to the Board of Civil Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Kangxi he rose from first-class imperial guard to vice-minister of War for pursuit and apprehension, and was then moved to the Board of Civil Appointments.

sentences.zh: 十三年，命署前鋒統領，參贊定南將軍希爾根軍務。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was ordered to act as vanguard commandant and assist Pacification General Who Settles the South Hilgen in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was named acting vanguard commandant on the staff of Pacification General Who Settles the South Hilgen.

sentences.zh: 精忠遣將陷撫州，舒恕從希爾根進擊，克之。

translations.literal: Jingzhong sent generals who took Fuzhou; Shuxu followed Hilgen in an advance against them and captured the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingzhong's generals seized Fuzhou, Shuxu marched with Hilgen to retake it.

sentences.zh: 十四年，精忠兵復至，又擊破之，克新城、宜黃、崇仁、樂安諸縣。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Jingzhong's troops returned; he again defeated them and took the counties of Xincheng, Yihuang, Chongren, and Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, when Jingzhong's army came back, he routed them again and recovered Xincheng, Yihuang, Chongren, and Le'an.

sentences.zh: 上命舒恕援廣東，授鎮南將軍。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Shuxu to relieve Guangdong and appointed him Pacification General of the South.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Shuxu to reinforce Guangdong and made him Pacification General of the South.

sentences.zh: 叛將馬雄及三桂將王弘勳攻高州，與戰不利，退駐肇慶。

translations.literal: The rebel general Ma Xiong and Wu Sangui's general Wang Hongxun attacked Gaozhou; the battle went badly and he withdrew to camp at Zhaoqing.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel Ma Xiong and Wu Sangui's general Wang Hongxun struck Gaozhou, Shuxu fought them unsuccessfully and fell back to Zhaoqing.

sentences.zh: 十五年，尚之信反，再退駐贛州。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Zhixin rebelled, and he again withdrew to camp at Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, when Zhixin rose in rebellion, Shuxu retreated once more to Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 十六年，上命解鎮南將軍印授莽依圖，率師下廣東，令舒恕留兵佐巡撫佟國楨守贛州。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year the emperor stripped Shuxu of the Pacification General of the South seal and gave it to Mangyitu, who led an army south into Guangdong; Shuxu was ordered to leave troops to assist Governor Tong Guozhen in holding Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year the emperor transferred the Pacification General of the South seal from Shuxu to Mangyitu and sent Mangyitu into Guangdong; Shuxu was left with troops to help Governor Tong Guozhen hold Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋复授安南將軍。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was again appointed Pacification General of Annam.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon reappointed Pacification General of Annam.

sentences.zh: 三桂兵自宜章窺南雄、韶州，上命莽依圖赴韶州應敵，而舒恕守南雄為聲援。

translations.literal: Wu Sangui's troops from Yizhang threatened Nanxiong and Shaozhou; the emperor ordered Mangyitu to Shaozhou to meet the enemy, while Shuxu held Nanxiong as a supporting force.
translations.idiomatic: With Wu Sangui's troops probing Nanxiong and Shaozhou from Yizhang, the emperor sent Mangyitu to Shaozhou to meet them and left Shuxu at Nanxiong in support.

sentences.zh: 十七年，穆佔言郴州、桂陽新復，請敕舒恕移師駐守。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Muzhan reported that Chenzhou and Guiyang had been newly recovered and requested an edict that Shuxu move his army to garrison them.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Muzhan reported the recent recovery of Chenzhou and Guiyang and asked that Shuxu be ordered to move up and garrison the region.

sentences.zh: 舒恕疏言南韶為湖南、江西、廣東三省接壤，不可輕離。

translations.literal: Shuxu memorialized that Nanxiong and Shaozhou lay where Hunan, Jiangxi, and Guangdong met, and that he could not lightly leave them.
translations.idiomatic: Shuxu replied that Nanxiong and Shaozhou sat at the junction of Hunan, Jiangxi, and Guangdong and must not be abandoned.

sentences.zh: 繼命進次梧州。

translations.literal: He was next ordered to advance and encamp at Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was then ordered forward to Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 十八年，即軍前授都察院左都御史。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was appointed at the front Left Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he received appointment as Left Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate while still in the field.

sentences.zh: 旋與莽依圖共擊吳世琮，解南寧之圍。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he joined Mangyitu in attacking Wu Shizong and raised the siege of Nanning.
translations.idiomatic: He soon joined Mangyitu against Wu Shizong and lifted the siege of Nanning.

sentences.zh: 舒恕以病乞還肇慶，召還京。

translations.literal: Shuxu pleaded illness and asked to return to Zhaoqing; he was recalled to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Shuxu claimed illness and asked to withdraw to Zhaoqing; the court recalled him to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 入對，上察其神色如故，無病狀，詔詰責，命羈候宗人府，下王大臣議，奪職。

translations.literal: When he was received in audience the emperor observed that his appearance was unchanged and he showed no sign of illness; an edict rebuked him, ordered him detained awaiting judgment in the Imperial Clan Court, referred the case to princes and ministers for deliberation, and stripped him of office.
translations.idiomatic: At audience the emperor found him in full health despite his plea; Shuxu was rebuked by edict, held in custody at the Imperial Clan Court, referred to the princes and ministers for judgment, and dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，起鑲黃旗滿洲副都統，再遷寧夏將軍，參贊撫遠大將軍費揚古軍務，討噶爾丹。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year he was restored as Manchu deputy lieutenant-general of the Bordered Yellow Banner, then promoted to Ningxia general, assisting Grand General Who Pacifies the Distant Feiyanggu in military affairs against Galdan.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year he was recalled as Manchu deputy lieutenant-general of the Bordered Yellow Banner, then made Ningxia general on the staff of Grand General Who Pacifies the Distant Feiyanggu for the campaign against Galdan.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，上親征，授揚威將軍，從費揚古出西路。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year the emperor took the field in person; Shuxu was appointed General Who Displays Might and followed Feiyanggu on the western route.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor marched in person in the thirty-fifth year, Shuxu was named General Who Displays Might and took the western route under Feiyanggu.

sentences.zh: 上駐棟斯拉，召費揚古議軍事，以舒恕署大將軍。

translations.literal: When the emperor halted at Dongnisila he summoned Feiyanggu to discuss military affairs and had Shuxu act as grand general.
translations.idiomatic: While the emperor was encamped at Dongnisila he called Feiyanggu to council and left Shuxu as acting grand general.

sentences.zh: 師有功，予拖沙喇哈番世職，擢正藍旗滿洲都統。

translations.literal: Because the army had merit, he was granted the hereditary rank of captain and promoted to Manchu lieutenant-general of the Plain Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: For the army's success he received the hereditary captaincy and was raised to Manchu lieutenant-general of the Plain Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 以病乞休。

translations.literal: He pleaded illness and requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: He retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 勒貝，郭絡羅氏，滿洲正藍旗人，鄂羅塞臣子。

translations.literal: Lebei, of the Guoluoguo clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Blue Banner and the son of Eroluosechen.
translations.idiomatic: Lebei, of the Guoluoguo clan, belonged to the Plain Blue Banner and was the son of Eroluosechen.

sentences.zh: 初授侍衛，兼管牛錄事。

translations.literal: At first he was appointed bodyguard and also managed company affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He began as an imperial guard and concurrently managed his company.

sentences.zh: 累遷正藍旗滿洲都統。

translations.literal: He was promoted step by step to Manchu lieutenant-general of the Plain Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to Manchu lieutenant-general of the Plain Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 三桂亂未平，康熙十六年春，上以簡親王喇佈出師江西久無功，參贊均不勝任，命勒貝及哈克三、舒庫往代之。

translations.literal: With Wu Sangui's rebellion still unsettled, in the spring of the sixteenth year of Kangxi the emperor, because Prince Jian Labu had campaigned in Jiangxi for a long time without success and his staff officers had all proved incompetent, ordered Lebei together with Hakesan and Shuku to replace them.
translations.idiomatic: While Wu Sangui's rebellion still raged, the spring of Kangxi sixteen found Prince Jian Labu stalled in Jiangxi and his deputies wanting; the emperor sent Lebei, Hakesan, and Shuku to take over.

sentences.zh: 既，命與江寧將軍額楚守韶州；

translations.literal: Subsequently he was ordered to hold Shaozhou together with Jiangning General Echu;
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was ordered to defend Shaozhou with Jiangning General Echu;

sentences.zh: 又詔進次梧州，與弘烈攻鬱林及北流、興業、陸川、博白，軍益振，乘勝下南寧，克象州。

translations.literal: an edict then ordered him to advance to Wuzhou and, with Honglie, attack Yulin and the counties of Beiliu, Xingye, Luchuan, and Bobai; the army's morale rose, and pressing the victory he descended on Nanning and took Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: then to push on to Wuzhou and, with Fu Honglie, strike Yulin, Beiliu, Xingye, Luchuan, and Bobai—the army's spirits soared, and riding the momentum he took Nanning and Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 十九年秋，莽依圖卒於軍。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the nineteenth year Mangyitu died in camp.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the nineteenth year Mangyitu died on campaign.

sentences.zh: 詔勒貝代為鎮南將軍，從賚塔定雲南。

translations.literal: An edict had Lebei replace him as Pacification General of the South and follow Laita in pacifying Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Lebei was ordered to succeed him as Pacification General of the South and join Laita in the conquest of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 抵西隆，诇知三桂將何繼祖等屯安籠所石門坎，與瑪奇率前鋒奮攻，次第克三峰，奪隘口，復安籠所。

translations.literal: Reaching Xilong, he learned through scouts that Wu Sangui's generals He Jizu and others were encamped at Shimengkan in Anlong Prefecture; with Maqi he led the vanguard in a fierce assault, took three peaks in succession, seized the pass, and recovered Anlong Prefecture.
