translations.literal: The rebels probed Jinhua; he dispatched Deputy Lieutenant-General Woshen, Vice General Chen Shikai, and others to drive them back;
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels tested Jinhua he sent Deputy Lieutenant-General Woshen, Vice General Chen Shikai, and others to beat them back;

sentences.zh: 复犯台州，寧波、紹興皆騷動。

translations.literal: They again attacked Taizhou, and Ningbo and Shaoxing were both thrown into turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Then they struck Taizhou, and Ningbo and Shaoxing were both thrown into alarm.

sentences.zh: 上命康親王杰書為大將軍，貝子傅喇塔為寧海將軍，統師援浙，拉哈達以都統參贊軍務。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Prince Kang Jieshu to serve as grand general and Prince Fulata as Pacification General of Ninghai to lead armies to aid Zhejiang; Lahada was made lieutenant-general assisting in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor named Prince Kang Jieshu grand general and Prince Fulata Pacification General of Ninghai to reinforce Zhejiang; Lahada served as a lieutenant-general on the staff.

sentences.zh: 十四年，擊處州賊，連下松陽、宣平。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he attacked the rebels at Chuzhou and in succession took Songyang and Xuanping.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he struck the rebels at Chuzhou and took Songyang and Xuanping in succession.

sentences.zh: 十五年，從康親王徇福建。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he followed Prince Kang in subduing Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he followed Prince Kang on the Fujian campaign.

sentences.zh: 精忠降，即導我師攻鄭錦。

translations.literal: Jingzhong surrendered and then guided our army against Zheng Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jingzhong submitted, he showed the imperial armies the way against Zheng Jing.

sentences.zh: 時漳州、泉州、興化三府為錦所據，遣其將許耀以三萬人偪福州，拉哈達率師擊之，破其壘十四。

translations.literal: At that time the three prefectures of Zhangzhou, Quanzhou, and Xinghua were held by Jing; he sent his general Xu Yao with thirty thousand men to threaten Fuzhou; Lahada led troops to attack him and broke fourteen of his forts.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangzhou, Quanzhou, and Xinghua were then all in Zheng Jing's hands; he dispatched Xu Yao with thirty thousand men against Fuzhou. Lahada met him in the field and smashed fourteen of his camps.

sentences.zh: 其冬，傅喇塔卒於軍，授拉哈達寧海將軍。

translations.literal: That winter Fulata died in camp and Lahada was appointed Pacification General of Ninghai.
translations.idiomatic: When Fulata died in camp that winter, Lahada was named Pacification General of Ninghai.

sentences.zh: 十六年，與賚塔合軍攻興化，克之，其將郭維籓以仙遊降。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he united with Laita to attack Xinghua, captured it, and its general Guo Weifan surrendered Xianyou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he joined Laita in assaulting Xinghua and took the city; Guo Weifan handed over Xianyou in surrender.

sentences.zh: 耀奔泉州，复據以堅守。

translations.literal: Yao fled to Quanzhou, recovered it, and held on stubbornly.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yao fled to Quanzhou, seized it again, and dug in for a hard defense.

sentences.zh: 拉哈達率銳師宵加之，漏未盡，梯入，斬耀及諸偽官，入城撫定軍民。

translations.literal: Lahada led elite troops in a night attack; before the night watches had ended he scaled the walls with ladders, beheaded Yao and the various pseudo-officials, entered the city, and pacified the soldiers and civilians.
translations.idiomatic: Lahada stormed the city by night with crack troops, escalading before dawn, cut down Xu Yao and the puppet officials, and entered to calm soldiers and civilians alike.

sentences.zh: 是時錦連敗，還廈門，泉州、漳州二府及海澄等十縣皆复，降將四百、兵四千有奇。

translations.literal: At that time Jing had suffered repeated defeats and returned to Xiamen; the two prefectures of Quanzhou and Zhangzhou and ten counties including Haicheng were all recovered; there were more than four hundred surrendering generals and more than four thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: By then Zheng Jing, beaten again and again, had withdrawn to Xiamen; Quanzhou, Zhangzhou, and ten counties including Haicheng came back under control, along with more than four hundred defecting commanders and four thousand-odd troops.

sentences.zh: 移師略潮州，叛將劉進忠亦降，乃還守福州。

translations.literal: He shifted the army to reduce Chaozhou; the rebel general Liu Jinzhong also surrendered, and then he returned to guard Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He turned his army toward Chaozhou; the rebel general Liu Jinzhong capitulated as well, and he then went back to hold Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 十七年，錦將劉國軒陷海澄，复犯泉州，斷萬安、江東二橋，扼長泰、同安諸隘，南北援絕，泉州幾不守。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Jing's general Liu Guoxuan took Haicheng and again attacked Quanzhou, cut the two bridges at Wan'an and Jiangdong, and held the passes at Changtai and Tong'an; relief from north and south was severed, and Quanzhou was almost lost.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Liu Guoxuan, a general of Zheng Jing, seized Haicheng and struck Quanzhou again, wrecking the Wan'an and Jiangdong bridges and sealing the passes at Changtai and Tong'an so that north and south could not reinforce each other; Quanzhou came close to falling.

sentences.zh: 拉哈達駐漳州，詔責其不亟援海澄，趣戴罪赴泉州難。

translations.literal: Lahada was garrisoned at Zhangzhou; an edict reproached him for not urgently relieving Haicheng and ordered him to proceed to Quanzhou's crisis while under obligation to atone for his crime.
translations.idiomatic: Lahada was posted at Zhangzhou; the emperor rebuked him for failing to rescue Haicheng in time and bade him redeem himself by racing to Quanzhou's aid.

sentences.zh: 拉哈達議自長泰入，會江漲，軍阻水。

translations.literal: Lahada planned to enter from Changtai, but encountered rising river waters and the army was blocked by flood.
translations.idiomatic: Lahada intended to advance from Changtai, but the rivers swelled and his army was stopped by the floodwaters.

sentences.zh: 侍讀學士李光地方居憂在籍，乃遣使導師出間道，自南靖道漳平趨安溪，遂薄泉州，圍乃解。

translations.literal: Reader-in-Waiting Li Guangdi was at home in mourning in his native place; he then sent envoys to guide the army out by a hidden path, from Nanjing county by way of Zhangping toward Anxi, and thus pressed near Quanzhou, and the siege was then lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangdi, a Reader-in-Waiting, was mourning at home in his native district; he sent guides to lead the army by a back trail from Nanjing county through Zhangping toward Anxi, closing on Quanzhou from an unexpected quarter until the siege was raised.

sentences.zh: 國軒築壘濱海東石地，當金門、廈門道。

translations.literal: Guoxuan built stockades on the coastal ground at Dongshi, blocking the route to Kinmen and Xiamen.
translations.idiomatic: Guoxuan threw up fortifications at coastal Dongshi, squatting across the approaches to Kinmen and Xiamen.

sentences.zh: 十八年，拉哈達遣沃申攻克之。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Lahada dispatched Woshen to attack and capture it.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year Lahada sent Woshen to storm and take the position.

sentences.zh: 十九年，與巡撫吳興祚自同安至潯尾，分兵渡海，拉哈達居中，興祚自左，總兵王英自右，並趨廈門。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, with Governor Wu Xingzuo he went from Tong'an to Xunwei, divided forces to cross the sea; Lahada was in the center, Xingzuo on the left, Regional Commander Wang Ying on the right, and all together pressed on Xiamen.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he and Governor Wu Xingzuo marched from Tong'an to Xunwei, split their forces for the crossing—Lahada in the center, Xingzuo on the left, Regional Commander Wang Ying on the right—and converged on Xiamen.

sentences.zh: 賚塔與總督姚啟聖，提督萬正色、楊捷，總兵黃大來師來會，三面合擊，賊不能支，遂克廈門。

translations.literal: Laita, together with Governor-General Yao Qisheng, Provincial Military Commissioners Wan Zhengse and Yang Jie, and Regional Commander Huang Dalai, came with armies to rendezvous; attacking from three sides in concert, the rebels could not hold and Xiamen was thus captured.
translations.idiomatic: Laita joined Governor-General Yao Qisheng, Provincial Military Commissioners Wan Zhengse and Yang Jie, and Regional Commander Huang Dalai; a three-pronged assault broke the rebels' resistance and Xiamen fell.

sentences.zh: 復進攻金門，其將吳國俊等迎降，錦與國軒走歸台灣。

translations.literal: Advancing again to attack Kinmen, its generals Wu Guojun and others came out to surrender; Jing and Guoxuan fled back to Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing on to Kinmen, they accepted the surrender of Wu Guojun and other commanders while Zheng Jing and Guoxuan fled back to Taiwan.

sentences.zh: 詔召康親王還京，命拉哈達與副都統馬思文守福州。

translations.literal: An edict summoned Prince Kang back to the capital and ordered Lahada and Deputy Lieutenant-General Masiven to guard Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The court recalled Prince Kang to the capital and left Lahada and Deputy Lieutenant-General Masiven to hold Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，撤滿洲兵還京，追論失守海澄罪，部議降世職為三等，並罷官，上以拉哈達從康親王平福建有勞，留都統任。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year the Manchu troops were withdrawn to the capital; his offense in losing Haicheng was reviewed afterward, and the Board deliberated reducing his hereditary rank to the third class and dismissing him from office, but the emperor noted that Lahada had merit in following Prince Kang in pacifying Fujian and kept him in his lieutenant-general post.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year the Manchu garrison was recalled to the capital and Lahada was called to account for losing Haicheng; the Board recommended demoting his hereditary rank to third class and removing him from office, but the emperor credited his service under Prince Kang in pacifying Fujian and allowed him to remain lieutenant-general.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，致仕。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he retired.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，病卒，卹如製。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year he died of illness; condolences were paid as prescribed.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness in the forty-second year; the court granted the customary posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 察哈泰，薩克達氏，滿洲鑲紅旗人，世居寧古塔。

translations.literal: Cihatai, of the Sakda clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Red Banner whose family had long lived at Ningguta.
translations.idiomatic: Cihatai, of the Sakda clan, was a Bordered Red Banner Manchu whose family had long been settled at Ningguta.

sentences.zh: 事太宗，從伐明，屢有功。

translations.literal: He served Taizong, followed campaigns against Ming, and repeatedly won merit.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taizong he joined the campaigns against Ming and won distinction again and again.

sentences.zh: 順治初，逐李自成，討金聲桓，皆在行間，屢擢太僕寺理事官，並授三等阿達哈哈番。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shunzhi he followed the pursuit of Li Zicheng and the suppression of Jin Shenghuan, serving in the ranks throughout; he was repeatedly promoted to director of affairs at the Court of the Imperial Stud and was also granted the hereditary rank of third-class commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In early Shunzhi he marched against Li Zicheng and helped suppress Jin Shenghuan, fighting in the front ranks throughout; he rose repeatedly at the Court of the Imperial Stud and was granted a third-class hereditary commandantship.

sentences.zh: 复遷太僕寺卿、鑲紅旗滿洲副都統。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and Manchu deputy lieutenant-general of the Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and Manchu deputy lieutenant-general of the Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 從伐俄羅斯，將舟師，招降斐雅喀百二十餘戶。

translations.literal: Following the campaign against Russia, he commanded the river fleet and induced more than one hundred and twenty Feiyaka households to submit.
translations.idiomatic: On the Russian campaign he led the river force and brought more than one hundred and twenty Feiyaka households over in submission.

sentences.zh: 坐所部戰艦戰失利，奏不實，罷副都統，奪世職，專管牛錄事。

translations.literal: Because the warships under his command were defeated in battle and his memorial was untrue, he was dismissed as deputy lieutenant-general, stripped of his hereditary office, and put in charge of company affairs alone.
translations.idiomatic: When his fleet was beaten and his report proved false, he lost his deputy lieutenant-generalship and hereditary rank and was reduced to managing a company alone.

sentences.zh: 康熙三年，复授鑲紅旗蒙古副都統。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kangxi he was again appointed Mongol deputy lieutenant-general of the Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Kangxi he was restored as Mongol deputy lieutenant-general of the Bordered Red Banner.

sentences.zh: 以老乞休，上慰留之。

translations.literal: Because of age he begged to retire; the emperor comforted him and kept him in office.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded age and asked to retire; the emperor reassured him and bade him stay on.

sentences.zh: 尋遷護軍統領，加太子少保。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was transferred to commander of the Guards and given the title Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made commander of the Guards and named Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 十三年，從拉哈達出駐兗州。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he followed Lahada out to garrison at Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he marched out with Lahada to garrison Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 上命拉哈達赴杭州，以敕印留付察哈泰，繼為鎮東將軍。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Lahada to proceed to Hangzhou and left the commission seal with Cihatai, who then succeeded as General Who Pacifies the East.
translations.idiomatic: When Lahada was sent to Hangzhou, the emperor left the commission seal with Cihatai, who took over as General Who Pacifies the East.

sentences.zh: 十四年，命仍以護軍統領帥所部赴荊州，聽順承郡王勒爾錦調度。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was ordered to continue as commander of the Guards and lead his troops to Jingzhou, taking orders from Prince of Shuncheng Le'erjin.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he remained commander of the Guards, led his division to Jingzhou, and served under Prince of Shuncheng Le'erjin.

sentences.zh: 十五年，三桂將陶繼智等犯宜昌，率兵駐江陵，通聲援。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Wu Sangui's generals Tao Jizhi and others invaded Yichang; he led troops stationed at Jiangling to maintain communications and lend support.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, when Wu Sangui's generals Tao Jizhi and others struck Yichang, he posted troops at Jiangling to keep lines open and stand ready to reinforce.

sentences.zh: 七月，卒於軍，卹如製。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he died in camp; condolences were paid as prescribed.
translations.idiomatic: He died in camp in the seventh month; the court granted the customary posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 察哈泰調赴荊州，上命以鎮東將軍印授副都統布顏，統蒙古兵留駐兗州。

translations.literal: When Cihatai was transferred to Jingzhou, the emperor ordered the seal of General Who Pacifies the East conferred on Deputy Lieutenant-General Buyan to command the Mongol troops remaining garrisoned at Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cihatai's transfer to Jingzhou brought Buyan the seal of General Who Pacifies the East and command of the Mongol garrison left at Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 事定，撤還京師。

translations.literal: When the situation was settled, the troops were withdrawn back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Once order was restored, the garrison was recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 根特，納喇氏，滿洲正黃旗人。

translations.literal: Gente, of the Nara clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Gente, of the Nara clan, belonged to the Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 父達雅里，國初來歸。

translations.literal: His father Dayali came over in submission at the founding of the dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: His father Dayali submitted when the dynasty was first established.

sentences.zh: 從伐明，攻深州，先登，克之。

translations.literal: Following campaigns against Ming, he attacked Shenzhou, was first to scale the walls, and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: On the Ming campaigns he assaulted Shenzhou, was first over the wall, and took the city.

sentences.zh: 軍功，累進一等參將世職。

translations.literal: For military merit he was repeatedly advanced to the hereditary rank of first-class vice general.
translations.idiomatic: Battle honors raised him in stages to a first-class hereditary vice generalship.

sentences.zh: 根特早歲從戎，數立功績。

translations.literal: Gente took up arms in his youth and repeatedly won distinction.
translations.idiomatic: Gente entered service young and piled up honors in the field.

sentences.zh: 從伐明，攻泗水縣、定州，並先登，賜號「巴圖魯」，授三等甲喇章京世職。

translations.literal: Following campaigns against Ming, he attacked Sishui county and Dingzhou, was first to scale the walls in both, was granted the title "Baturu," and was appointed to the hereditary rank of third-class company commander.
translations.idiomatic: On the Ming campaigns he stormed Sishui county and Dingzhou, first over the wall in each, earned the title "Baturu," and received a third-class hereditary company commandership.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，授刑部理事官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi he was appointed director of affairs at the Board of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shunzhi he was made a director of affairs at the Board of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 五年，金聲桓以南昌叛，從大將軍譚泰討之，薄南昌，攻未下，根特自城南以登，拔之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Jin Shenghuan rebelled at Nanchang; following Grand General Tan Tai in suppressing him, they pressed close to Nanchang but could not take it; Gente escaladed from the south and captured the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, when Jin Shenghuan rose at Nanchang, Gente followed Grand General Tan Tai against him; the siege stalled until Gente went up the southern wall and broke the city.

sentences.zh: 聲桓中矢死，擒王得仁。

translations.literal: Shenghuan was struck by an arrow and died; Wang Deren was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Shenghuan took an arrow and died; Wang Deren was taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 師還，擢梅勒額真，進一等阿達哈哈番。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was promoted to banner commandant and advanced to first-class commandant.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return he was made banner commandant and raised to first-class commandant.

sentences.zh: 六年，姜瓖以大同叛，其黨虞允、白漳、張萬全陷蒲州及臨晉、猗氏、河津。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Jiang Xiang rebelled at Datong; his partisans Yu Yun, Bai Zhang, and Zhang Wanquan seized Pu prefecture together with Linjin, Yishi, and Hejin.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Jiang Xiang rebelled at Datong; his followers Yu Yun, Bai Zhang, and Zhang Wanquan overran Pu prefecture and the counties of Linjin, Yishi, and Hejin.

sentences.zh: 從總督孟喬芳濟河擊之，复蒲城，進徵平陽。

translations.literal: Following Governor-General Meng Qiaofang he crossed the Yellow River to strike them, recovered Pucheng, and advanced to campaign at Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the Yellow River with Governor-General Meng Qiaofang, retook Pucheng, and pushed on toward Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 白漳擁步騎六千至榮河迎戰，奮擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Bai Zhang led six thousand infantry and cavalry to Ronghe to give battle; Gente struck fiercely and routed them.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Zhang brought six thousand foot and horse to meet him at Ronghe; Gente charged hard and broke them.

sentences.zh: 迫黃河，賊未及濟，師薄之，賊多赴水死，遂斬白漳，餘奔吉鎮，悉殲焉。

translations.literal: Pressing them to the Yellow River before the rebels could cross, the army closed on them; many rebels drowned in the water; Bai Zhang was then beheaded, and the remainder fled to Jizhen and were annihilated to the last.
translations.idiomatic: He drove them to the Yellow River before they could ford; many drowned as his troops closed in, Bai Zhang was beheaded, and the survivors who fled to Jizhen were wiped out.

sentences.zh: 移師趨猗氏，瓖黨衛登芳依山結寨，與萬全為犄角，復分兵擊斬萬全，殲其眾。

translations.literal: Shifting the army toward Yishi, Jiang's partisan Wei Dengfang held a stockade on the mountain in mutual support with Wanquan; he again divided troops, struck and beheaded Wanquan, and annihilated his force.
translations.idiomatic: Turning toward Yishi, he found Jiang's follower Wei Dengfang entrenched on the hills in concert with Wanquan; he split his force, killed Wanquan, and destroyed that column.

sentences.zh: 尋生得登芳，復進敗瓖黨郭中傑於聞喜。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Dengfang was captured alive; advancing again, he defeated Jiang's partisan Guo Zhongjie at Wenxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Dengfang was soon taken alive; pressing forward, he routed Jiang's partisan Guo Zhongjie at Wenxi.

sentences.zh: 康熙十三年，吳三桂反，命出駐兗州。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Kangxi, when Wu Sangui rebelled, he was ordered out to garrison at Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sangui rebelled in the thirteenth year of Kangxi, he was posted to garrison Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋以江西地要衝，命偕副都統席布徙守南昌。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, because Jiangxi was a vital crossroads, he was ordered together with Deputy Lieutenant-General Xibu to shift and guard Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi's strategic weight soon brought an order for him and Deputy Lieutenant-General Xibu to relocate and hold Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 長沙陷，袁州、吉安二府與接壤，巡撫董衛國請發兵駐防，命根特自南昌移師，備戰禦。

translations.literal: When Changsha fell, the two prefectures of Yuanzhou and Ji'an bordered the rebel territory; Governor Dong Weiguo requested that troops be sent to garrison them, and Gente was ordered to move his army from Nanchang to prepare for battle and defense.
translations.idiomatic: After Changsha fell, Yuanzhou and Ji'an prefectures lay on the rebel frontier; Governor Dong Weiguo asked for a garrison, and Gente was ordered to shift from Nanchang and stand ready to fight.

sentences.zh: 尋以希爾根為定南將軍，根特參贊軍務。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Hilgen was made Pacification General Who Settles the South, and Gente assisted in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Hilgen was soon named Pacification General Who Settles the South, with Gente on his staff.

sentences.zh: 尚可喜疏請兵，上令根特俟希爾根兵至，率所部下廣東。

translations.literal: Shang Kexi memorialized requesting troops; the emperor ordered Gente to wait until Hilgen's army arrived and then lead his own troops down into Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: When Shang Kexi pleaded for reinforcements, the emperor told Gente to hold until Hilgen arrived, then march his division into Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 耿精忠反，授根特平寇將軍，令仍返江西。

translations.literal: When Geng Jingzhong rebelled, Gente was appointed Pacification General Who Subdues Bandits and ordered to return again to Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Jingzhong's revolt brought Gente the seal of Pacification General Who Subdues Bandits and orders to turn back to Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 副將柯升以廣信叛應精忠，破都昌，窺南康，復命根特先定廣信，與前鋒統領覺羅舒恕自袁州規長沙。

translations.literal: Vice General Ke Sheng rebelled at Guangxin in response to Jingzhong, broke Duchang, and eyed Nankang; the emperor again ordered Gente first to settle Guangxin, while Vanguard Commander Aisin Gioro Shuxu, starting from Yuanzhou, aimed at Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Vice General Ke Sheng rose at Guangxin for Jingzhong, stormed Duchang, and menaced Nankang; the court ordered Gente to secure Guangxin first while Vanguard Commander Aisin Gioro Shuxu advanced from Yuanzhou toward Changsha.

sentences.zh: 是年八月，卒於軍，卹如製。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of that year he died in camp, and posthumous honors were granted according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: That eighth month he died in the field, and the court granted the customary posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書哈爾哈齊副定南將軍希爾根駐江西，根特卒，上命以平寇將軍印授之。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Harhaqi served as deputy to Pacification General Who Settles the South Hilgen, garrisoned in Jiangxi; when Gente died, the emperor ordered the Pacification General Who Quells Rebels seal conferred upon him.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Rites Harhaqi was deputy to Pacification General Who Settles the South Hilgen in Jiangxi; when Gente died, the emperor gave him the Pacification General Who Quells Rebels seal.

sentences.zh: 十一月，命赴江寧，贊大將軍簡親王軍務，鎮江南。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he was ordered to proceed to Jiangning to assist Grand General Prince Jian Labu in military affairs and guard Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he was sent to Jiangning to serve on Grand General Prince Jian Labu's staff and hold Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 十五年五月，命率江寧兵赴廣東，授華善平寇將軍，道江西，命會師攻吉安。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fifteenth year he was ordered to lead Jiangning troops to Guangdong and was appointed Pacification General Who Quells Rebels; passing through Jiangxi he was ordered to join forces and attack Ji'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fifteenth year the emperor ordered him to lead Jiangning forces into Guangdong and named him Pacification General Who Quells Rebels; marching through Jiangxi he was told to unite his column with others and strike Ji'an.

sentences.zh: 螺子山之敗，坐奪官，披甲。

translations.literal: For the defeat at Luozi Mountain he was stripped of rank for the offense and donned armor.
translations.idiomatic: After the rout at Luozi Mountain he lost his commission for the fault and was reduced to common soldier's service.

sentences.zh: 華善，漢軍正白旗人。

translations.literal: Huashan was a Han bannerman of the Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Huashan belonged to the Plain White Han Army Banner.

sentences.zh: 石廷柱第三子，為豫親王多鐸壻，授和碩額駙。

translations.literal: He was the third son of Shi Tingzhu; as son-in-law of Prince of Yu Dodo he was appointed prince consort.
translations.idiomatic: The third son of Shi Tingzhu, he married Prince of Yu Dodo's daughter and received appointment as prince consort.

sentences.zh: 三桂反，授安南將軍，守鎮江。

translations.literal: When Wu Sangui rebelled he was appointed Pacification General of Annam and ordered to guard Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sangui rose in rebellion he was named Pacification General of Annam and posted to guard Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 尋命贊大將軍簡親王軍務，駐江寧。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to assist Grand General Prince Jian Labu in military affairs and was garrisoned at Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon placed on Grand General Prince Jian Labu's staff and stationed at Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 十五年，改授平寇將軍。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was reassigned as Pacification General Who Quells Rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was given the Pacification General Who Quells Rebels appointment.

sentences.zh: 十六年，簡親王進軍江西，命華善率所部從，以平寇將軍印留付江寧副都統科爾擴岱。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year Prince Jian Labu advanced into Jiangxi; Huashan was ordered to follow with his own command, leaving the Pacification General Who Quells Rebels seal with Jiangning Deputy Lieutenant-general Ko'erkedai.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, when Prince Jian Labu marched into Jiangxi, Huashan was told to bring his troops along but leave the Pacification General Who Quells Rebels seal with Jiangning deputy lieutenant-general Ko'erkedai.

sentences.zh: 十七年，授定南將軍，命守茶陵。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was appointed Pacification General Who Settles the South and ordered to guard Chaling.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was made Pacification General Who Settles the South and assigned to hold Chaling.

sentences.zh: 三桂兵攻永興急，上命簡親王進次茶陵，而令華善救永興。

translations.literal: Wu Sangui's troops pressed the attack on Yongxing hard; the emperor ordered Prince Jian Labu to advance and encamp at Chaling while Huashan was sent to relieve Yongxing.
translations.idiomatic: With Wu Sangui's forces hammering Yongxing, the emperor ordered Prince Jian Labu forward to Chaling and told Huashan to save the city.

sentences.zh: 華善不敢進，上切責之，解將軍印，令從穆佔自效。

translations.literal: Huashan dared not advance; the emperor sharply rebuked him, stripped him of the general's seal, and ordered him to follow Muzhan and redeem himself through service.
translations.idiomatic: Huashan hung back; the emperor rebuked him sternly, removed his general's seal, and ordered him to serve under Muzhan and win redemption in the field.

sentences.zh: 事平，論罪，上命寬之。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled his guilt was reviewed; the emperor ordered leniency.
translations.idiomatic: After peace was restored his case came up for judgment, and the emperor showed mercy.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，卒。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the thirty-fourth year.

sentences.zh: 子石文炳，襲廷柱三等伯。

translations.literal: His son Shi Wenbing inherited Tingzhu's third-class earldom.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shi Wenbing succeeded to Shi Tingzhu's third-class earldom.

sentences.zh: 累遷福州將軍。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Fuzhou general.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in stages to Fuzhou general.

sentences.zh: 以華善老，召授正白旗漢軍都統。

translations.literal: Because Huashan was old, he was recalled and appointed lieutenant-general of the Plain White Han Army Banner.
translations.idiomatic: When Huashan grew old he was called back to the capital and made lieutenant-general of the Plain White Han Army Banner.

sentences.zh: 尋聞喪還京，卒於途。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, on hearing of a bereavement he returned toward the capital and died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: He soon learned of a death in the family and started back for the capital, but died on the way.

sentences.zh: 席卜臣，瓜爾佳氏，滿洲鑲白旗人，費英東弟郎格之孫也。

translations.literal: Xibochen, of the Guwalgiya clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered White Banner and a grandson of Fei Yingdong's younger brother Langge.
translations.idiomatic: Xibochen, of the Guwalgiya clan, belonged to the Bordered White Banner and was a grandson of Langge, younger brother of Fei Yingdong.

sentences.zh: 事太宗，從上徵朝鮮。

translations.literal: He served the Taizong and followed the emperor in the campaign against Korea.
translations.idiomatic: He entered Hong Taiji's service and followed the throne in the expedition against Korea.

sentences.zh: 從睿親王多爾袞伐明，戰於通州，擊敗太監高起潛軍；

translations.literal: Following Prince Regent Dorgon he campaigned against Ming, fought at Tongzhou, and defeated the army of the eunuch Gao Qiqian;
translations.idiomatic: He marched with Prince Regent Dorgon against Ming, fought at Tongzhou, and routed the eunuch Gao Qiqian's force;

sentences.zh: 再從攻錦州，屢戰破敵。

translations.literal: again following in the attack on Jinzhou, he repeatedly fought and broke the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: he again joined the siege of Jinzhou and won repeated victories in the field.

sentences.zh: 順治初，從大軍入關擊李自成，戰於一片石，遂至慶都，敗賊於太原。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shunzhi he followed the great army through the pass against Li Zicheng, fought at Yipianshi, then reached Qingdu and defeated the bandits at Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In early Shunzhi he crossed the pass with the main army against Li Zicheng, fought at Yipianshi, pressed on to Qingdu, and routed the rebels at Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 二年，從英親王阿濟格徇陝西，逐自成至安陸。

translations.literal: In the second year he followed Prince of Ying Ajige in a sweep through Shaanxi and pursued Zicheng as far as Anlu.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he campaigned through Shaanxi under Prince of Ying Ajige and chased Zicheng to Anlu.

sentences.zh: 三年，從肅親王豪格下四川，殲張獻忠。

translations.literal: In the third year he followed Prince Su Haoge south into Sichuan and destroyed Zhang Xianzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he entered Sichuan with Prince Su Haoge and helped destroy Zhang Xianzhong.

sentences.zh: 五年，從討叛將薑瓖。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he followed in the suppression of the rebel general Jiang Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he took part in suppressing the rebel general Jiang Xiang.

sentences.zh: 敘功，屢遇恩詔，世職至二等拜他喇布勒哈番，官至護軍統領。

translations.literal: His merits were recorded; repeatedly benefiting from amnesties, his hereditary office rose to second-class baturu, and he reached the post of guard commandant.
translations.idiomatic: When honors were reviewed he was raised again and again under grace edicts to second-class baturu, and he rose to commandant of the guard.

sentences.zh: 十二年，與都統卓洛等出駐荊州，破孫可望。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he went out with Lieutenant-general Zhuoluo and others to garrison Jingzhou and defeated Sun Kewang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he marched with Lieutenant-general Zhuoluo and others to garrison Jingzhou and broke Sun Kewang.

sentences.zh: 十六年，與安南將軍明安達里援江寧，敗鄭成功將楊文英等，斬馘甚多。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, with Pacification General of Annam Mingandali he reinforced Jiangning, defeated the generals of Zheng Chenggong including Yang Wenying, and took many heads.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he reinforced Jiangning with Pacification General of Annam Mingandali, routed Zheng Chenggong's generals Yang Wenying and others, and took many heads.

sentences.zh: 康熙九年，擢鑲白旗蒙古都統。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Kangxi he was promoted Mongol lieutenant-general of the Bordered White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Kangxi he was made Mongol lieutenant-general of the Bordered White Banner.

sentences.zh: 十二年，加太子少傅。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was given the additional title Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he received the additional title of Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 十三年，吳三桂反，上授都統赫葉為安西將軍，與西安將軍瓦爾喀等自漢中下四川。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Wu Sangui rebelled; the emperor appointed Lieutenant-general Heyeh Pacification General of Anxi, and with Xi'an General Warka and others he entered Sichuan from Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, when Wu Sangui rebelled, the emperor named Lieutenant-general Heyeh Pacification General of Anxi and sent him into Sichuan from Hanzhong with Xi'an general Warka and others.

sentences.zh: 十四年，复授席卜臣鎮西將軍，與副都統巴喀、德業立同駐西安。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Xibochen was again appointed Pacification General of the West and, with Deputy Lieutenant-generals Baka and Deyeli, was jointly garrisoned at Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year Xibochen was again made Pacification General of the West and stationed at Xi'an with deputy lieutenant-generals Baka and Deyeli.

sentences.zh: 尋又命大將軍貝​​勒洞鄂西討，赫葉歸將軍印，參贊軍務。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Grand General Prince Beile Tonge was again ordered on a western campaign; Heyeh returned the general's seal and assisted in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor soon sent Grand General Prince Beile Tonge west on campaign; Heyeh surrendered the general's seal and served as staff officer.

sentences.zh: 是冬，席卜臣與赫葉會師攻保寧。

translations.literal: That winter Xibochen and Heyeh joined forces and attacked Baoning.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Xibochen united with Heyeh and besieged Baoning.

sentences.zh: 三桂將王屏籓拒守，師屯蟠龍山，屏籓出戰，潛遣別將自他道絕流渡，撓我師，我師棄營退，席卜臣引還漢中。

translations.literal: Wu Sangui's general Wang Pingfan held out in defense; the army encamped at Panlong Mountain; Pingfan came out to fight and secretly sent another commander by another route to ford the river against the current and harass our army; our army abandoned camp and withdrew, and Xibochen led the retreat back to Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui's general Wang Pingfan held the city while our army encamped on Panlong Mountain. Pingfan gave battle, then secretly sent another officer by a side route to ford the river upstream and harry our lines; our forces abandoned camp and fell back, and Xibochen withdrew to Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 上命覈諸將罪，赫葉奪職，披甲自效。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the generals' crimes reviewed; Heyeh was stripped of office, donned armor, and sought to redeem himself through service.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered an accounting of the generals' faults: Heyeh lost his post, donned armor, and was sent to redeem himself in the ranks.

sentences.zh: 方軍退，佐領穆舒誓死決戰，將甲上記號付將軍，督兵奮鬥。

translations.literal: Just as the army was retreating, company commander Mushu vowed to fight to the death, handed the insignia on his armor to the general, and led the troops in fierce combat.
translations.idiomatic: As the army was pulling back, company commander Mushu swore to stand and die, gave his armor insignia to the general, and rallied the men for a desperate fight.

sentences.zh: 上聞，超擢正紅旗蒙古副都統，以獎其勇。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of this he was exceptionally promoted to Mongol deputy lieutenant-general of the Plain Red Banner to reward his courage.
translations.idiomatic: On hearing of it the emperor jumped him to Mongol deputy lieutenant-general of the Plain Red Banner in reward for his bravery.

sentences.zh: 席卜臣至漢中，值王輔臣叛，棧道絕，餉不繼，引還西安。

translations.literal: When Xibochen reached Hanzhong, Wang Fuchen rebelled, the plank roads were cut, supplies failed to follow, and he led the army back to Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: Xibochen had barely reached Hanzhong when Wang Fuchen rebelled, the plank roads were severed, and supplies ran out; he withdrew to Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 旋召還京。

translations.literal: He was soon recalled to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon called back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 事定，王大臣追論蟠龍山戰敗罪，奪官，削世職。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled, the princes and grand ministers reviewed in retrospect the crime of defeat at Panlong Mountain; he was stripped of office and his hereditary rank was removed.
translations.idiomatic: After peace returned, a board of princes and grand ministers reopened the Panlong Mountain defeat; he lost his post and his hereditary title.

sentences.zh: 上以席卜臣有勞，免其籍沒。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Xibochen had prior merit, exempted him from confiscation of property.
translations.idiomatic: Because Xibochen had earlier services to his credit, the emperor spared his estate from confiscation.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: He soon died.
translations.idiomatic: He died not long afterward.

sentences.zh: 希爾根，覺爾察氏，滿洲正黃旗人，世居長白山。

translations.literal: Hilgen, of the Jogiorca clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner whose family had long lived at Changbai Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Hilgen, of the Jogiorca clan, belonged to the Plain Yellow Banner; his family were longtime residents of Changbai Mountain.

sentences.zh: 太宗居籓邸時，任護衛。

translations.literal: When the Taizong still resided at his princely establishment he served as bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: While Hong Taiji still held his princely residence, Hilgen served in his guard.

sentences.zh: 天聰間，以軍功授牛錄章京世職。

translations.literal: During the Tiancong era, for military merit he was granted the hereditary office of company commander.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tiancong reign he earned a hereditary company commandership for his battlefield service.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年，從伐明，連下昌平、寶坻十餘城，遷巴牙喇甲喇章京。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongde he followed the campaign against Ming, took more than ten cities including Changping and Baodi in succession, and was transferred to vanguard deputy commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongde he joined the expedition against Ming, captured Changping, Baodi, and more than ten other towns in turn, and was promoted to vanguard deputy commandant.

sentences.zh: 擊敗明太監高起潛兵，擒總兵巢丕昌，又助譚泰設伏，敗三屯營騎兵。

translations.literal: He defeated the troops of the Ming eunuch Gao Qiqian, captured regional commander Chao Pichang, and also assisted Tan Tai in setting an ambush and defeating the cavalry of the Santunying camp.
translations.idiomatic: He routed the eunuch Gao Qiqian's force, took regional commander Chao Pichang prisoner, and helped Tan Tai lay an ambush that broke the Santunying cavalry.

sentences.zh: 師還，敵躡後，諸將護輜重先行，希爾根殿，超授一等甲喇章京世職。

translations.literal: When the army returned, the enemy followed close on the rear; the generals escorted the baggage train ahead, and Hilgen brought up the rear; he was extraordinarily promoted to the hereditary office of first-class deputy commandant.
translations.idiomatic: On the march home the enemy pressed the rear; while other officers shepherded the baggage train forward, Hilgen covered the withdrawal and was promoted out of turn to a hereditary first-class deputy commandant.

sentences.zh: 二年，從克皮島。

translations.literal: In the second year he followed in the capture of Pi Island.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he joined the reduction of Pi Island.

sentences.zh: 將行圍，選扈從，其父雅賴與焉。

translations.literal: When a hunting enclosure was about to be held, escorts were selected, and his father Yalai was among them.
translations.idiomatic: When the court prepared a battue, Yalai, his father, was chosen for the escort retinue.

sentences.zh: 希爾根向睿親王多爾袞乞免，不許，紿以珠爾堪代之。

translations.literal: Hilgen begged Prince Regent Dorgon for exemption on his father's behalf; permission was not granted, and he deceived them by saying Zhu Erkan would serve in his place.
translations.idiomatic: Hilgen pleaded with Prince Regent Dorgon to spare his father; when refused, he falsely promised that Zhu Erkan would take Yalai's place.

sentences.zh: 事覺，坐欺罔，應罷官奪世職，從寬論罰鍰。

translations.literal: When the matter came to light he was convicted of deception; he should have been dismissed and stripped of his hereditary office, but a lenient penalty of fine was imposed instead.
translations.idiomatic: Exposure brought a charge of deceit; though dismissal and loss of his hereditary rank were prescribed, he was leniently fined instead.

sentences.zh: 從師圍錦州，壁山岡，明兵至，擊走之，並擊退松山援兵。

translations.literal: Following the army in the siege of Jinzhou, he fortified a hill ridge; when Ming troops arrived he struck and drove them off, and also beat back the relief force from Songshan.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the siege of Jinzhou and held a ridge line; Ming reinforcements were beaten off, including the relief column from Songshan.

sentences.zh: 复坐擅離軍伍、言事不實，停敘功。

translations.literal: Again he was convicted of leaving his unit without authorization and reporting matters falsely; merit reckoning was suspended.
translations.idiomatic: He was again found guilty of quitting his unit without leave and filing false reports, and his service credits were held in abeyance.

sentences.zh: 七年，師圍薊州，明總兵白騰蛟率師馳救，希爾根擊敗之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the army besieged Jizhou; Ming regional commander Bai Tengjiao led troops in haste to relieve it, and Hilgen defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, when the army invested Jizhou, Ming regional commander Bai Tengjiao rushed to its relief; Hilgen routed him.

sentences.zh: 順治二年，從英親王阿濟格討李自成，圍延安，大敗其眾。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi he followed Prince of Ying Ajige in suppressing Li Zicheng, besieged Yan'an, and inflicted a great defeat on his forces.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shunzhi he campaigned under Prince of Ying Ajige against Li Zicheng, invested Yan'an, and shattered his army.

sentences.zh: 其將有一隻虎者，稱驍果，數犯我師。

translations.literal: Among his generals was one called One-Tiger, renowned for ferocity, who repeatedly assailed our army.
translations.idiomatic: One of Zicheng's commanders, nicknamed One-Tiger, was famed for fierceness and struck at our columns again and again.

sentences.zh: 希爾根三戰皆克，遂至西安。

translations.literal: Hilgen won all three engagements and then reached Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: Hilgen won three straight fights and pushed through to Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 自成奔湖廣，逐北至安陸，賊據城拒戰，復與鼇拜攻克之，獲戰艦八十艘。

translations.literal: Zicheng fled to Huguang; pursuing him north as far as Anlu, the bandits held the city and resisted; Hilgen again together with Oboi stormed and took it, capturing eighty warships.
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng fled into Huguang; Hilgen chased him north to Anlu, where the rebels held the city; with Oboi he took the town and seized eighty war junks.

sentences.zh: 引兵武昌，賊又集艦五百浮江將東下，譚泰率眾往取，希爾根先至，獲之，進三等梅勒章京。

translations.literal: Leading troops to Wuchang, he found the bandits had again assembled five hundred ships intending to float downriver eastward; Tan Tai led the army to seize them, and Hilgen arrived first and captured them, advancing to third-class banner commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Marching toward Wuchang, he found five hundred rebel vessels preparing to sail downriver; Tan Tai was sent to seize them, Hilgen got there first and captured the fleet, and was raised to third-class banner commandant.

sentences.zh: 三年，從肅親王豪格徵張獻忠，與哈寧阿、阿爾津、蘇拜敗之西充。

translations.literal: In the third year he followed Prince Su Haoge in campaigning against Zhang Xianzhong and, with Haning'a, Arjin, and Subai, defeated him at Xichong.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he entered Sichuan with Prince Su Haoge against Zhang Xianzhong and, with Haning'a, Arjin, and Subai, routed him at Xichong.

sentences.zh: 別趨涪州，討賊袁韜，斬虜多。

translations.literal: Detaching toward Fu prefecture he suppressed the bandit Yuan Tao and killed or captured many.
translations.idiomatic: He then swung toward Fu prefecture against the rebel Yuan Tao and killed or captured a great many.

sentences.zh: 尋坐哈寧阿陷重圍不救，復與阿爾津等爭功，論棄市，詔改罰贖，降三等甲喇章京。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was convicted for failing to rescue Haning'a when the latter was trapped in heavy encirclement, and again for disputing merit with Arjin and others; death by dismemberment at the marketplace was proposed, but an edict commuted the sentence to ransom and reduced him to third-class deputy commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon found guilty of leaving Haning'a trapped without relief and of quarreling with Arjin and others over credit; though condemned to execution, an edict commuted the sentence to a fine and demoted him to third-class deputy commandant.

sentences.zh: 六年，姜瓖叛據大同，希爾根從巽親王滿達海討之，圍太谷，以砲破其城，斬瓖所署置知縣李成沛、都司吳汝器，進克大同。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Jiang Xiang rebelled and held Datong; Hilgen followed Prince Xun Mandahai in suppressing him, besieged Taigu, battered the city with cannon, beheaded Li Chengpei and Wu Ruqi, the county magistrate and assistant commander Jiang had installed, and advanced to capture Datong.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Jiang Xiang seized Datong; Hilgen marched with Prince Xun Mandahai against him, bombarded Taigu into submission, beheaded Jiang's appointees Li Chengpei and Wu Ruqi, and pressed on to take Datong.

sentences.zh: 以次復長子縣，渾源、朔二州。

translations.literal: In succession he recovered Changzi county and the two prefectures of Hunyuan and Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: Changzi county and the prefectures of Hunyuan and Shuo fell to him in turn.

sentences.zh: 永寧州、嵐縣、潞安府並降。

translations.literal: Yongning prefecture, Lan county, and Lu'an prefecture all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Yongning prefecture, Lan county, and Lu'an prefecture all submitted.

sentences.zh: 又與漢岱攻复遼州。

translations.literal: He again with Handai attacked and recovered Liaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: With Handai he next retook Liaozhou.

sentences.zh: 山西平，當進秩，因訴前鐫秩冤，累遇恩詔，進一等阿達哈哈番。

translations.literal: When Shanxi was pacified he was due for advancement in rank, but because he appealed the injustice of an earlier demotion, and repeatedly benefited from grace edicts, he was advanced to first-class commandant.
translations.idiomatic: With Shanxi pacified he was due for promotion, but appealed an earlier wrongful demotion; successive amnesties restored him to first-class commandant.

sentences.zh: 九年，擢巴牙喇纛章京，列內大臣。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was elevated to vanguard banner commander and listed among the inner ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he became vanguard banner commander and took a seat among the inner ministers.

sentences.zh: 十二年，加太子太保。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was given the additional title of Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he received the additional rank of Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 十三年，耿精忠叛，使其將白顯忠寇廣信、建昌、撫州，授希爾根定南將軍，率師援江西，以桑格贊軍事，沃赫、伊巴罕從，次南昌，而三城已陷。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Geng Jingzhong rebelled and sent his general Bai Xianzhong to raid Guangxin, Jianchang, and Fuzhou; Hilgen was appointed Pacification General Who Settles the South, led an army to relieve Jiangxi, with Sange assisting in military affairs and Wohe and Yibahan following; when he reached Nanchang the three cities had already fallen.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Geng Jingzhong rebelled and sent Bai Xianzhong against Guangxin, Jianchang, and Fuzhou; Hilgen was named Pacification General Who Settles the South and marched into Jiangxi with Sange on his staff and Wohe and Yibahan in his train, but by the time he reached Nanchang all three cities were lost.

sentences.zh: 是時安親王岳樂駐師省城，檄希爾根先取撫州，賊出拒，連敗之，並率沙納哈擊走援賊，城賊待援不至，棄城走。

translations.literal: At that time Prince An Yuele was stationed with his army at the provincial capital and ordered Hilgen first to take Fuzhou; the bandits came out to resist and were defeated repeatedly, and Hilgen also led Shanahai to drive off the relief rebels; the rebels in the city, waiting for relief that did not come, abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Prince An Yuele held the provincial capital and ordered Hilgen to retake Fuzhou first; the rebels sallied and were beaten again and again, and Hilgen sent Shanahai to scatter their relief force; the garrison, seeing no rescue come, abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 精忠將陳昇構土賊郭應定等犯贛州，令副都統甘度海御之，大捷。

translations.literal: Jingzhong's general Chen Sheng incited the local brigands Guo Yingding and others to attack Ganzhou; Hilgen ordered Deputy Lieutenant-general Ganduhai to meet them and won a great victory.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhong's officer Chen Sheng stirred up local bandits led by Guo Yingding against Ganzhou; Hilgen sent Deputy Lieutenant-general Ganduhai to meet them and won a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 追至龍泉，破三壘，復攻取曹林十餘寨。

translations.literal: Pursuing as far as Longquan, he broke three stockades and again attacked and took more than ten stockades at Caolin.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued the enemy to Longquan, stormed three camps, and went on to seize more than a dozen stockades around Caolin.

sentences.zh: 十四年，擊敗精忠將邵連登，復建昌。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he defeated Jingzhong's general Shao Liandeng and recovered Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he routed Jingzhong's general Shao Liandeng and retook Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 移師饒州，擊退餘幹、浮梁、樂平諸縣賊。

translations.literal: Shifting his army to Raozhou, he struck and drove off the bandits of the counties of Yugan, Fuliang, and Leping.
translations.idiomatic: Moving on Raozhou, he drove rebel bands out of Yugan, Fuliang, Leping, and the neighboring counties.

sentences.zh: 會岳樂師下湖南，命簡親王喇布赴南昌，以希爾根副之。

translations.literal: When Yuele's army descended into Hunan, Prince Jian Labu was ordered to proceed to Nanchang, with Hilgen as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuele's column pushed into Hunan, Prince Jian Labu was sent to Nanchang with Hilgen as his second.

sentences.zh: 三桂將高大節出醴陵、萍鄉，陷吉安，冀斷岳樂軍後路。

translations.literal: Wu Sangui's general Gao Dajie came out from Liling and Pingxiang, took Ji'an, and hoped to cut off the rear of Yuele's army.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui's general Gao Dajie marched from Liling and Pingxiang, seized Ji'an, and aimed to sever Yuele's line of retreat.

sentences.zh: 我師屯螺子山，大節勇，常以少騎奔我師。

translations.literal: Our army encamped at Luozi Mountain; Dajie was brave and often charged our army with a small body of cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Our forces held Luozi Mountain; Dajie was a bold fighter and repeatedly harried our camp with small cavalry raids.

sentences.zh: 喇布倉皇棄營走，希爾根從之，賊入壘，縱飲飽掠而歸。

translations.literal: Labu in panic abandoned camp and fled, and Hilgen followed him; the bandits entered the stockade, drank freely, plundered their fill, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Labu panicked, abandoned camp, and fled, and Hilgen followed; the rebels overran the entrenchments, feasted, looted at leisure, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 俄大節死，希爾根督師攻圍，戰又弗勝。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Dajie died; Hilgen directed the army in attack and siege, but again could not win in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Dajie soon died, and Hilgen took command of the siege, but the assaults still failed.

sentences.zh: 逾歲賊遁，詔仍駐南昌。

translations.literal: After more than a year the bandits fled; an edict ordered him to remain garrisoned at Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later the rebels gave up and withdrew; the court ordered him to stay on at Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 尋以老召還。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, on account of age, he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Age soon brought orders to return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 十八年，卒。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighteenth year.

sentences.zh: 子喀西泰，任護軍參領。

translations.literal: His son Kashitai served as guard company commander.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kashitai held the post of guard company commander.

sentences.zh: 從征四川，攻保寧，死蟠龍山之戰。

translations.literal: Following a campaign into Sichuan he attacked Baoning and died in the battle of Panlong Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the Sichuan expedition against Baoning and was killed at Panlong Mountain.

sentences.zh: 論曰：當三籓亂時，命將四出，以庶姓授大將軍，惟圖海與賚塔二人而已。

translations.literal: The commentary states: during the rebellion of the Three Feudatories, when generals were dispatched in all directions, among common-clan appointments to grand general there were only Tu Hai and Laita.
translations.idiomatic: The historian remarks: when the Three Feudatories rose, commanders were sent out on every front, yet only two men of common birth received the grand general's seal—Tu Hai and Laita.

sentences.zh: 賚塔自廣西，穆佔自湖南，皆轉戰下雲南，削平巨憝，功最多。

translations.literal: Laita from Guangxi and Muzhan from Hunan both fought their way down into Yunnan, overthrew the arch rebel, and their merit was greatest.
translations.idiomatic: Laita from Guangxi and Muzhan from Hunan each fought their way into Yunnan and brought down the chief rebel; their services stood above all others.

sentences.zh: 穆佔功歸彰泰，故賞不逮；

translations.literal: Muzhan's merit was credited to Zhangtai, and therefore his rewards did not measure up;
translations.idiomatic: Muzhan's victories were reckoned to Zhangtai's account, so his rewards never matched his deeds;

sentences.zh: 賚塔、莽依圖功與相並，惜中道先卒。

translations.literal: Laita and Mangyitu had merit equal to his, but regrettably both died on campaign before the end.
translations.idiomatic: Laita's and Mangyitu's records rivaled his own, though both died on campaign before the war was won.

sentences.zh: 佛尼埒等皆夙將，有戰績。

translations.literal: Fonilie and the others were veterans of long service and had battle records.
translations.idiomatic: Fonilie and his fellows were seasoned commanders with long lists of victories.

sentences.zh: 其時雜號將軍，或出朝命，或即軍前除拜。

translations.literal: At that time the assorted titled generals might be appointed by court edict or promoted on the spot at the front.
translations.idiomatic: The various ad hoc generalships of that era were filled either by court appointment or by field promotion on the spot.

sentences.zh: 有一人遞掌二三印者，有一印迭授二三人者，皆領異軍獨當一路。

translations.literal: Some men successively held two or three seals, and some seals were passed in turn among two or three men; each commanded a separate army and held a front alone.
translations.idiomatic: One man might hold two or three seals in succession; one seal might pass among two or three men—each commanded an independent force on his own axis of advance.

sentences.zh: 綜而觀之，當日行師應敵之大概，可以得其要矣。

translations.literal: Taken together, one may grasp the essentials of how armies marched and met the enemy in that time.
translations.idiomatic: Viewed as a whole, these cases reveal the essential pattern of how armies of that day marched, fought, and answered the enemy.
